correctness_confidence.basis: All explicit formulas in Theorems 1–3, Krein and absolute-bound polynomials, moment-line equations, and all 16 rational rows of Table 1 check out exactly by independent hand calculation. However, Section 3 prose falsely claims Diophantine constraint (9) isolates a single infinite polynomial family (refuted by r=a, s=-(a+1)(4a+1)^2, m_s=4a(a+1)), Theorem 2(c) is unproved inside the PDF, Theorem 1(a) skips why irrational SRGs are conference graphs, and Figure 3(a) mislabels Schläfli's c_1 line (-15/2 - 5c_3) as c_2.

rigor.basis: Although Theorems 1(b), 2(a)–(b), and 3(a) contain sound polynomial algebra, proof rigor in the PDF has serious gaps: Theorem 2(c) (n<=1200) gives zero mathematical proof and delegates solely to external cert04; Table 1 moment-line derivations are deferred to cert01/cert09–15; Theorems 1(a) and 2(a) omit proving irrational SRGs are conference graphs; Section 3 falsely claims (9) isolates one family; and t>=3 feasible parameter tuples are treated as SRGs despite unproved graph existence.

novelty.basis: A modest, reactive follow-up to Kang's October 2026 moment-line preprint [9] and Godsil [7]. Rationality of M_hat is already known in full generality [7], and 16-vertex Hadamard IUM on Clebsch, L_2(4), and Shrikhande is known [3,8]. The genuinely new contributions—the closed-form off-diagonal imbalance/Seidel midpoint law (Thm 1b), the feasible t-family generalizing Ternary Golay (Thm 2b), and its universal UAM moment-line no-go proof (Thm 3a)—are clean but use only elementary quadratic and low-degree polynomial algebra.

significance.basis: Specialized, incremental contribution to continuous-time quantum walk mixing on strongly regular graphs. Separating off-diagonal Cesàro uniformity from UAM via an explicit feasible parameter family anchored by the ternary Golay graph is a neat structural observation, and the conference extremality barrier is crisp. However, the Cesàro return barrier ~1/2 > 1/n was essentially known, no new actual graphs are shown to exist for t>=3 (n>=676), and the paper provides no new general analytic or combinatorial techniques.

reproducibility.basis: The paper includes a concrete public GitHub URL and release tag (v1.0.0) in the page-1 footnote and names internal Lean theorems and certificate IDs (cert01–cert15). However, despite prominently advertising '16 SHA-256 certificates' under certificates/MANIFEST.json, not a single SHA-256 digest or commit hash appears anywhere in the PDF. Moreover, Theorem 2(c) and Table 1 cannot be reproduced from the PDF alone, as the search algorithm, explicit adjacency matrices (e.g. L_2(4) vs Shrikhande), and derivations are omitted.

assessments.summary: This 9-page paper studies Cesàro average mixing and generalized uniform average mixing (UAM) of continuous-time quantum walks on primitive strongly regular graphs SRG(n,k,λ,μ), directly following up Godsil [7] and Kang's October 2026 moment-line preprint [9]. All explicit algebraic identities, Krein/absolute-bound checks, moment lines, and all 16 Table 1 entries verify cleanly from first principles. Nevertheless, the mathematical depth is modest and elementary—relying on Bose–Mesner quadratic identities and low-degree polynomial expansions—and major revision is needed for four substantive reasons. First, Section 3 materially overclaims that Diophantine constraint (9) 'isolates a single infinite polynomial family': (9) actually admits a second infinite polynomial family r=a, s=-(a+1)(4a+1)^2, m_s=4a(a+1) (producing n=289, 2401, ...), and no uniqueness proof is given for n>1200 even under Krein/absolute bounds. Second, Theorem 2(c) (n<=1200) and Table 1 lack self-contained proofs in the PDF, deferring to unprinted certificates; Theorem 1(a)/2(a) also omit proving irrational SRGs are conference graphs. Third, graph existence for the t-family is unproved for t>=3 (only feasible parameters). Fourth, Figure 3(a) mislabels Schläfli's c_1 curve as c_2, and zero SHA-256 hashes appear in the PDF.
strengths: All explicit algebraic formulas in Theorems 1–3, Krein K1/K2 expansions, absolute-bound polynomials, moment lines, and all 16 rational entries of Table 1 are exact and cleanly verified.
Clean structural characterization of off-diagonal Cesàro imbalance via 2(n-2k+lambda-mu)/(n*Delta), complement sign-flip, and Seidel eigenvalue midpoint condition in Theorem 1(b).

Explicit feasible polynomial t-family (10) anchored by the Ternary Golay dual coset graph (t=2) showing that off-diagonal Cesàro uniformity does not imply generalized UAM across the entire family (Theorem 3(a)).
Clear separation between [-1,1]^3 polytope nonemptiness (necessary for UAM) and trigonometric moment-curve realizability (Remark 1), and accurate inclusion of concrete GitHub URL and tag v1.0.0.
weaknesses: Reactive 1-month follow-up to Kang [9] (Oct 2026) relying entirely on elementary Bose–Mesner quadratic algebra and degree-<=5 polynomial expansions; rationality of M_hat [7] and 16-vertex Hadamard IUM [3,8] are already known.

Material overclaim in Section 3 that Diophantine system (9) isolates a single infinite polynomial family, disproved by a second infinite polynomial family (producing n=289, 2401, ...), with no classification proof beyond n<=1200.
Heavy reliance on external code/certificates instead of self-contained proofs in the PDF for Theorem 2(c) and Table 1, plus absence of any SHA-256 hashes in the PDF.
Unproved graph existence for the polynomial t-family when t>=3 (n>=676) and minor mislabeling in Figure 3(a) ('Schlaefli c_2' vs c_1).
potential_errors: Section 3 prose (p. 4) claims Diophantine constraint n-2k+lambda-mu=0 'isolates a single infinite polynomial family', which is false: system (9) admits a second infinite polynomial family r=a, s=-(a+1)(4a+1)^2, m_s=4a(a+1), k=4a(a+1)(2a+1)(4a+1), n=2k-a+(a+1)(4a+1)^2 (a>=1; giving n=289, 2401, ...) with square Delta and integer multiplicities, plus multiple Pell branches for composite a(a+1). Even under Krein/absolute filtering, uniqueness is unproved for n>1200.

Theorem 2(c) (exhaustive classification for 5<=n<=1200) has no mathematical proof in the PDF ('follows directly from Certificate cert04'), even though reducing to k = ab + sqrt(ab(a+1)(b-1)) with a<=16, ab<300 yields an elementary human proof.

Figure 3(a) legend and caption (p. 8) label the plotted red curve (-15/2 - 5c_3 <= -5/2) as 'Schlaefli c_2', whereas for Schlaefli SRG(27,16,10,8) we have c_1(c_3) = -15/2 - 5c_3 <= -5/2 and c_2(c_3) = -8 - (9/2)c_3 <= -7/2 (c_1 and c_2 swap only on the complement SRG(27,10,1,5)).

Proof of Theorem 1(a) checks irrational rationality only for 'irrational conference graphs' without proving every primitive SRG with irrational eigenvalues is a conference graph (though Galois conjugation over Q(sqrt(Delta)) works directly), and Proof of Theorem 2(a) states Delta is a perfect integer square without proving it.

Theorem 2(b) and Theorem 3(a) call the t-family (t>=1) an infinite family of off-diagonal uniform SRGs, whereas graph existence is only known at t=2 (Ternary Golay) and unproved for all t>=3 (n=676, 1445, ...), where only feasible SRG parameters are established.
strong_novelty_candidates: Closed-form off-diagonal Cesàro mixing imbalance law 2(n-2k+lambda-mu)/(n*Delta), its complement sign-flip, and its equivalence to the Seidel regular eigenvalue bisecting the non-trivial Seidel eigenvalues (Theorem 1(b)).

Infinite feasible non-conference off-diagonal Cesàro-uniform SRG parameter family n(t)=(t+1)(4t+1)^2, k(t)=t(2t+1)(4t+3) anchored at t=2 by the Ternary Golay graph, with exact Krein (all t>=1) and absolute-bound (t>=2) verification (Theorem 2(b)).
Unconditional empty-polytope UAM no-go proof across all t>=1 of the off-diagonal Cesàro-uniform family (max c_1(c_3) <= -12 < -1), separating off-diagonal Cesàro uniformity from UAM (Theorem 3(a)).
unresolved_material_objections: Material overclaim in Section 3 prose (p. 4): Diophantine system (9) does NOT 'isolate a single infinite polynomial family'. A second infinite polynomial family r=a, s=-(a+1)(4a+1)^2, m_s=4a(a+1), k=4a(a+1)(2a+1)(4a+1), n=2k-a+(a+1)(4a+1)^2 (a>=1, yielding n=289, 2401, ...) solves (9) identically with square Delta and integer multiplicities (only failing Krein/absolute bounds), and even with Krein/absolute filtering no uniqueness proof is given for n>1200.

Missing mathematical proofs in the PDF: Theorem 2(c) (classification for 5<=n<=1200) has zero mathematical proof in the manuscript, relying entirely on unprinted Certificate cert04; similarly Theorem 3(c) / Table 1 omit derivations in favor of external certificates, and Theorems 1(a) and 2(a) omit proving that non-conference primitive SRGs have rational/integer eigenvalues.
Conflation of feasible SRG parameter tuples with actual graphs for t>=3 in Theorems 2(b) and 3(a): graph realization is known only at t=2 (Ternary Golay) and unproved for t>=3 (n=676, 1445, ...).

Minor figure/reproducibility defects in the PDF: Figure 3(a) legend/caption mislabels Schläfli's c_1 line (-15/2 - 5c_3) as 'Schläfli c_2' (actual c_2 is -8 - 9c_3/2 <= -7/2), and despite advertising '16 SHA-256 certificates', zero SHA-256 digests or commit hashes appear anywhere in the PDF.

Moreover, the paper does not resolve the genuinely open minimal-dimension threshold (whether n=4..7 admit rank-2 complex violations) or whether any real rank-2 counterexample exists in any dimension.

assessments.summary: This reactive follow-up to Chalmers (arXiv:2611.23269, Nov 2026) studies rank-2 Hermitian PSD matrices A = uu* + vv* for the Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue inequality per(A)I_n - F_A >= 0. Its substantive verified contributions are: (1) an O(n^3) Cauchy-Binet elementary-symmetric-polynomial Gram decomposition of F_A (Theorem 1(c)), (2) an exact closed-form circulant Fourier spectrum on n-th roots of unity proving an AM-GM upper bound (n-1)^(-1/n) < 1 for n >= 3 (Theorem 2(c)), and (3) explicit rank-2 Gaussian-integer counterexamples at n = 8, 9, 10 (including compact A9 = J9 + z9 z9* with exact integer gap +11,572,992), which independently verify as genuine violations. However, the paper has serious mathematical, scholarly, and completeness defects barring acceptance as written. Page 2 reverses the implication between the 1985 Hadamard inequality and (1), misattributes (1) to Bapat-Sunder (1985) and Drury (2016, n=7) while omitting Bapat-Sunder (1986) and Drury (2018, n=16), and the Title/Abstract overclaim resolving 'the sharp rank-2 regime' despite leaving n = 4..7 (complex) and n >= 4 (real rank-2) open. Theorem 2(b) mislabels a rank <= 2 operator as 'exact rank-2' (false for z = (1,0,0)^T), uses undefined/inconsistent ()_perp notation, and omits proofs of D2(u) and D2(u) >= 0. Finally, cert10's vectors and all SHA-256 hashes are absent from the PDF.
strengths: Explicit, zero-float Gaussian-integer rank-2 complex counterexamples to per(A)I_n - F_A >= 0 at n = 8, 9, 10 (cert08, cert09, cert11), with printed integer coordinates, exact permanents, and verified positive integer Rayleigh gaps (and compact A9 = J9 + z9 z9* with per(A9) = 6,088,320 and gap +11,572,992).

Clean, self-contained derivation of the exact circulant Fourier eigenvalues lambda_m = n^2 (m-1)!(n-1-m)! r^{2m} on n-th roots of unity and the sharp weighted AM-GM barrier sup_{r>0} lambda_max(F_{A_n(r)}|_{1^perp})/per(A_n(r)) = (n-1)^{-1/n} < 1 for all n >= 3 (Theorem 2(c)).

Exact O(n^3) Cauchy-Binet elementary-symmetric-polynomial Gram factorization F_A = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} k!(n-1-k)!(U_k U_k^* + V_k V_k^*) over any subring R subseteq C (Theorem 1(c)), together with exact diagonal congruence invariance F_{DAD*} = |det D|^2 F_A (Theorem 1(b)) and the n=3 shift-Laplacian identity (Theorem 2(b), Eq. (7)).
Exact direct-sum and balanced real saturation family A = 2(J_m oplus J_m) achieving lambda_max(F_A|_{1^perp})/per(A) = 1 (Theorem 2(d)), plus rigorous centering improvement analysis (Theorem 3(d)).
Concrete GitHub repository URL with version tag (v1.0.0) provided in the manuscript footnote.
weaknesses: Reactive follow-up to Chalmers (arXiv:2611.23269, Nov 2026) on an already-refuted conjecture; Theorems 1 and 2(a),(b),(d) consist of elementary 2-to-10-line algebraic identities rather than deep new analytic methods.

Compressed or incomplete derivations in Theorem 1(b) (omits proving per(A) > 0), Theorem 2(b) (omits derivation of D2(u), omits proving D2(u) >= 0, skips U(2) rotation for u_i = 0), and Theorem 2(c) (omits monotonicity justification for n >= 5).

Theorem 3 delegates verification of 15-digit permanents and quadratic forms entirely to external Lean/Python artifacts rather than providing any human-verifiable calculation or exact lower-bound proof in the PDF, while reported spectral ratios and Figure 3(b) spectra are uncertified floats.

assessments.summary: This paper establishes deep topological, algebraic, and spectral boundaries for extending Huang-optimal matrix signings to general regular graphs and Cartesian products. It proves a universal complex torus-holonomy no-go theorem ruling out unitary solutions $S^2 = dI$ on Cartesian products of non-bipartite graphs, resolves the exact real-vs-complex signing dichotomy on complete graphs $K_q$ via symmetric conference and skew-Hadamard matrices, and introduces a non-bipartite Clifford-cube lifting recurrence. An exhaustive 11-graph switching-class atlas is verified via exact integer Faddeev-LeVerrier polynomials, rational Sturm isolation, and axiom-free Lean 4.36.0 formalization.

Exhaustively classifies real switching classes across 11 canonical regular graphs with zero-float arithmetic and Lean 4 formalization.

assessments.summary: This 9-page note studies Huang-optimal signings (S^2 = dI) over R and C for d-regular graphs and Cartesian products. Its cleanest original result (Theorem 1(a)) is an elementary 10-line proof that no Hermitian unit-modulus signing of G□H satisfies S^2 = (d_G + d_H)I when both G and H are non-bipartite, via 4-cycle plaquette cancellation on an odd-cycle torus, with a real Frobenius defect bound ||S^2 - dI||_F^2 >= 8v (Theorem 1(b), valid though loose vs 16v). Theorem 2(a) pairs classical symmetric conference-matrix constraints (q ≡ 2 mod 4) with the 2-line observation H_q = iA_q for skew-Hadamard matrices (q ≡ 0 mod 4), leaving general U(1) signings on K_q (e.g., q = 22) open despite 'Complex-vs-Real Dichotomy' framing. Theorem 2(b) applies Huang's block recursion to arbitrary Hermitian seeds G_0□Q_n without proving degree-bound tightness. Theorems 1(c) and 3 classify switching classes on 11 small graphs (n <= 10); independent checks confirm the core values in Table 1, yet the PDF proofs delegate exhaustiveness to external certificates without witness matrices or SHA-256 digests, and the Lean kernel checks only scalar arithmetic. A solid modest technical note needing revisions for self-containment and accuracy.
strengths: Theorem 1(a) provides a crisp, completely valid 10-line universal complex torus-holonomy no-go proof for Hermitian unit-modulus signings of G□H when both G and H are non-bipartite.

Independent first-principles algebraic checks confirm the exactness of key concrete results in Table 1, including the H(2,3) minimum-norm characteristic polynomial x(x^4 - 9x^2 + 16)^2, J(4,2), K_4, K_5, KG(5,2), C_5□K_2, and the A_16 skew-Hadamard doubling construction.

Section 5 transparently clarifies that the Lean 4.36.0 theorems formalize only the scalar arithmetic/modular kernel while matrix-level plaquette cancellation and Cauchy interlacing are proved in Sections 2-3.
weaknesses: Very modest mathematical depth relative to the paper's packaging: Theorem 1(a) is a 10-line signed-graph parity argument, Theorem 2(a)'s real part is classical 1933-1967 conference-matrix theory and its +-i part is a 2-line identity on skew-Hadamard matrices, Theorem 2(b) is Huang's exact 3-line block recursion from a non-zero seed, and Theorem 3 enumerates 11 tiny graphs (n <= 10, <= 1,024 switching classes).

The 20 Lean 4.36.0 theorems formalize only trivial scalar arithmetic and modular fragments (e.g. odd*odd parity, q = 4(a+delta)+2, 8v >= 8, and rational evaluation of x^2-x-4), not graph signings, matrices, or Cauchy interlacing.

No matching upper-bound constructions or tightness analysis are provided for Theorem 2(b)'s lifted threshold Delta((G_0□Q_n)[U]) >= ceil(sqrt(d_0 + n)) or for K_q (on K_q, the true bound is q/2 >> sqrt(q-1); on K_4□K_2, Delta >= 3 > 2 = ceil(sqrt(4))).
Frobenius defect bound 8v in Theorem 1(b) ignores the second diagonal of each +1 plaquette (which immediately gives 16v) and omits local triangle contributions.
potential_errors: Proof of Theorem 1(b) (p. 4): states identity (8) 'forces an even number of +1 or -1 plaquettes'; since m_1 m_2 is odd, the number of -1 plaquettes is even and the number of +1 plaquettes is necessarily odd (though the next clause correctly concludes at least one +1 plaquette exists).

Theorem 1(b) bound ||S^2 - dI||_F^2 >= 8v is valid but loose by a factor of 2: each +1 plaquette has two opposite vertex pairs, yielding 4 off-diagonal entries of magnitude 2 (16v), and for H(2,3) triangles add another 36 for a true floor of 52.

Proof of Theorem 2(a) (p. 5): Theorem 2(a) is stated for all q >= 2, but the proof checks odd q >= 3 and even q >= 4, omitting q = 2 (where both real +-1 and skew-Hadamard +-i signings exist, breaking the disjoint mod-4 narrative at q = 2).
Theorems 1 and 2 statements omit the 'simple' graph requirement (only introduced in Section 1), though Theorem 1's common-neighborhood size-2 argument requires simple graphs.

Theorem 3(b) and Table 1 list max lambda_5(C_5□K_2) only approximately as ~1.1756 instead of its exact algebraic value sqrt((5 - sqrt(5))/2), contradicting the paper's 'exact, zero-float' presentation.
Figure 1(b) plots eigenvalues in ascending rank order (1 to 9), opposite to the descending lambda_1 >= ... >= lambda_9 convention in the text, without stating this in the caption.
unresolved_material_objections: Non-self-contained proofs for Theorem 1(c) and Theorem 3: the PDF proofs delegate exhaustive classification, spectrum counts, and spectral extrema entirely to unprinted external Python scripts ('cert01-cert16') without supplying explicit witness signing matrices (e.g., for H(2,3) or J(4,2)), complete spectrum lists, or algebraic optimality proofs (which are elementary for several graphs like K_5 and Petersen), and leaves max lambda_5(C_5□K_2) as a decimal approximation (~1.1756) rather than its exact radical sqrt((5 - sqrt(5))/2), contradicting the claim of 'exact, zero-float algebraic proofs'.

Missing SHA-256 certificate hashes in the PDF: despite advertising '16 SHA-256 certificates under certificates/MANIFEST.json', no actual SHA-256 digests appear anywhere in the PDF, preventing independent cryptographic verification of the referenced v1.0.0 artifact from the paper itself.

Material framing overclaim on 'Complex-vs-Real Signing Dichotomy on K_q' and proof defects: the title, Section 3 heading, and Figure 2(a) frame the result as a complex-vs-real dichotomy on K_q (marking q = 22 as obstructed), whereas Theorem 2(a) restricts complex entries to purely imaginary {+-i} (skew-Hadamard matrices) and leaves general unit-modulus U(1) signings on K_q completely unresolved; additionally, Proof 1(b) falsely writes 'an even number of +1 or -1 plaquettes' (+1 count is odd), and Proof 2(a) omits the q = 2 case stated in the theorem.

assessments.summary: This paper advances the structural and algorithmic theory of sparse near-Monge matrices by resolving Open Problem 3 and Appendix D questions from Chen (2026). First, it introduces a symmetric vertex-cover cut partition that combines off-diagonal SMAWK sweeps with Wilber's doubling-phase algorithm for diagonal triangles, achieving an optimal O(s + n(tau + 1)) deterministic sequential DP bound with zero logarithmic factors. Second, it proves an exact signed-rectangle rank sandwich and an (n-2)^2 deterministic entry-oracle lower bound. Third, it tightens conditional hardness reductions via a unit-curvature triangular background and compresses envelope trees to O(r) internal nodes. All theorems are fully verified in constructive Lean 4.35.0 with zero sorries and supported by SHA-256 certificates.
strengths: Resolves Chen's Open Problem 3 with a zero-log O(s + n(tau + 1)) vertex-cover sequential DP algorithm.
Proves an exact signed-rectangle rank sandwich max([s/2], s_row, s_col) <= r_min <= s and an exact (n-2)^2 entry-oracle lower bound.
Introduces tight minimal strict curvature triangular-background compression saving Theta(n^{1-alpha}) weight.
Full machine-checked Lean 4.35.0 formalization with 0 sorry and 0 custom axioms.
weaknesses: As a reactive follow-up to a recent preprint, its scope is specialized, though executed with exceptional mathematical rigor.

correctness_confidence.basis: Core proofs of Theorems 2.3, 3.2, and 4.2(a)-(b) are sound, but material framing errors require revision: calling Theorem 2.3 'Optimal' without a lower bound (suboptimal vs. Chen Cor. 3.7 at s=tau=sqrt(n)), claiming a Fig. 2(b) speedup when Theorem 4.2(b) total complexity is Theta-unchanged for all r, omitting integrality in Def. 4.1, and imprecise 'exact (n-2)^2' / 's=0 or s<=2' wording in Thm. 3.2(c).

rigor.basis: Algebraic steps, block Monge invariance (Lem. 2.2), and Wilber's doubling invariant with arbitrary base potentials are verified cleanly. Minor rigor gaps include missing the integer-entry hypothesis in Def. 4.1 (used in Thm. 4.2a's proof), omitting strict-comparison tie-breaking for +inf in SMAWK, mislabeling 'Optimal' without a lower bound, inconsistent figure theorem numbering (Thm. 1-3 vs. 2.3-4.2), and loose 's=0 or s<=2' phrasing.

novelty.basis: Modest follow-up strictly scoped to Chen (arXiv:2611.34733v1). Symmetrizing vertex-cover cuts for SMAWK+Wilber DP (Thm. 2.3) is a neat trick achieving O(n(tau+1)) without logs, and compressing the static envelope tree to O(r) internal nodes with monotone-finger leaves (Thm. 4.2b) is a clean data-structure tweak. However, Thm. 3.2 and Thm. 4.2(a) rely on elementary calculations, and Thm. 4.2(b) leaves total asymptotic runtime unchanged.

significance.basis: Narrowly scoped extensions to a single 2026 preprint. Eliminating log^3 n factors in 1D DP for tau=O(1) given the negative-support list is a useful concrete speedup, though Theorem 2.3 is slower than Chen when tau >= log^3 n and s << n*tau. The rank sandwich, standard Omega(n^2) adversary bound, lambda_tri constant/active-index tightening, and O(r)-node tree (with identical overall asymptotic runtime) have limited broader impact.

reproducibility.basis: A concrete public GitHub repository URL appears in the page-1 footnote and file paths for Lean 4.35.0, zero-float verification, and 56 pytest tests are named in Section 5. However, despite prominently claiming 16 SHA-256 certificates and a manifest digest, zero SHA-256 hashes or commit SHAs appear in the PDF, and Lean theorem statements are absent (only algebraic/combinatorial invariants are listed as checked, not end-to-end DP/tree correctness).

assessments.summary: This follow-up to Chen (arXiv:2611.34733v1) studies near-Monge matrices with sparse negative adjacent mixed differences. Theorem 2.3 symmetrizes row and column cuts of a 2-approximate vertex cover into at most 2*tau+1 intervals, combining SMAWK and Wilber's algorithm (verified for arbitrary base potentials) to solve sequential 1D DP in O(s + n(tau+1)) time given the negative list, shaving Theta(log^3 n) off Chen's Corollary 3.7 for tau = O(1). Theorem 3.2 gives an elementary signed-rectangle rank sandwich (tight at s/2 and s) and an Omega(n^2) entry-oracle lower bound. Theorem 4.2 replaces (j-k)^2 by binom(j-k,2) in Chen's reduction and compresses Chen's envelope tree to O(r) internal nodes. While the core proofs are sound, the mathematical tools are modest and the PDF makes material overclaims: labeling Theorem 2.3 'Optimal' without a lower bound (and being slower than Chen's O((n+s)log^3 n) when s = tau = sqrt(n)), highlighting a speedup in Theorem 4.2(b)/Fig. 2(b) despite unchanged total asymptotic runtime across all r, overclaiming 'bit-weight blowup' compression while omitting integrality in Def. 4.1, and omitting all SHA-256/commit digests from the PDF.
strengths: Theorem 2.3 cleanly symmetrizes row and column vertex-cover cuts into a common ordered partition S of size <= 2*tau+2, proving block-wise Monge invariance (Lemma 2.2) and checking Wilber's doubling-phase invariant explicitly with arbitrary base potentials b(j) to solve sequential 1D DP in O(s + n(tau+1)) deterministic time given the negative-support list.
Eq. (9) gives an exact algebraic work identity sum_v (|J_v| + sum_{u<v}(|I_u|+|J_v|)) = mn <= (2*tau+1)n via |I_u| = |J_u|.

Theorem 3.2(a)-(b) cleanly derives the row/column-gap lower bounds max(ceil(s/2), max s_row, max s_col) <= r_min(C) <= s(C) with explicit tight witnesses at both s/2 and s, and Theorem 3.2(c) gives a valid Omega(n^2) randomized query lower bound via Yao's minimax principle.
Theorem 4.2(a) verifies the unit-curvature identity Delta M_tri = 1, active/padded dominance (22), and exact ceil(S_tilde/lambda_tri) recovery across positive, zero, and negative integers V.
Theorem 4.2(b) validly reduces the internal envelope tree size from 2n to O(r) internal nodes via elementary row blocks, static Monge concave-hull breakpoint arrays, and monotone leaf fingers.
weaknesses: All results are narrowly scoped reactive follow-ups to a single recent preprint (Chen, arXiv:2611.34733v1) using mostly elementary algebra, textbook adversary arguments, and standard classical DP algorithms (SMAWK 1987, Wilber 1988).
Theorem 2.3 requires the full negative-support list N_ut(C) as input and performs worse than Chen's Corollary 3.7 when tau is super-polylogarithmic and s << n*tau.

Theorem 4.2(b) reduces internal envelope-tree nodes to O(r) (still requiring O(n) space across leaf breakpoint arrays) without improving overall asymptotic time complexity over Chen's Theorem 3.4 in any regime.
Reproducibility verification from the PDF alone is incomplete: while a GitHub URL is given, no SHA-256 hashes, commit ID, or formal Lean theorem signatures are printed in the paper.

Minor presentation and precision defects throughout (malformed 's(C)=0 or s(C)<=2' phrasing, omitted +inf tie-breaking in SMAWK, missing integer hypothesis in Def. 4.1, and stale theorem numbering 'Thm. 1-3' inside Figures 1-2).
potential_errors: Theorem 2.3 Step 2 runs SMAWK on the strictly upper-triangular matrix G(i) + C(i, j) padded with +inf for i >= j; total monotonicity with +inf entries holds only if SMAWK breaks ties strictly in favor of smaller column indices (popping i_1 only on strict >), which is unstated.
Definition 4.1 writes A^(g), B^(g) in [-U, U] without restricting entries to integers, whereas Theorem 4.2(a)(i)-(ii) proofs explicitly require Delta B^(g) in Z and V in Z.

Theorem 3.2(c) states 'decides whether s(C)=0 (Monge) or s(C)<=2' (malformed since s(C)=0 implies s(C)<=2; clearly intends s(C)=0 vs. 1<=s(C)<=2 or s(C)=2) and calls (n-2)^2 an 'exact' deterministic lower bound even though boundary perturbations (e.g., +5*1_{(0,0)} giving s=1, r_min=1) make the true deterministic complexity n^2 (at n=3, (n-2)^2=1 is not tight).
Remark 2.4 notes Hopcroft-Karp in O(s*sqrt(tau)) reduces blocks from 2*tau+1 to tau+1, omitting that s*sqrt(tau) can exceed O(n(tau+1)) when s = Theta(n*tau).
Figure 1 and Figure 2 internal labels cite 'Thm. 1', 'Thm. 2', 'Thm. 3a', 'Thm. 3b' instead of Theorems 2.3, 3.2, 4.2a, 4.2b.
strong_novelty_candidates: Symmetric vertex-cover cut partition (Definition 2.1, Lemma 2.2, Theorem 2.3) combining greedy 2-approximate vertex cover with SMAWK and base-potential Wilber doubling-phase sweeps to eliminate all logarithmic factors in sequential 1D DP when tau(C) = O(1) (given the negative-support list).
unresolved_material_objections: Unproven and false-in-general 'Optimal' claim for Theorem 2.3: The title, Contribution 1, and Theorem 2.3 label the DP algorithm 'Optimal O(n(tau+1))' without stating or proving any Omega(n(tau+1)) lower bound. Whenever s << n*tau / log^3 n and tau = omega(log^3 n) (e.g., a matching of size s = tau = sqrt(n)), Theorem 2.3 takes O(n^{1.5}) whereas Chen's Corollary 3.7 takes O(n log^3 n), so Theorem 2.3 is strictly suboptimal outside tau = O(1) or dense s = Theta(n*tau).

Zero total asymptotic speedup in Theorem 4.2(b) and misleading Figure 2(b): The total time O(n*T_M*log n + r*log(r+2)*log n*(log n + T_M)) is Theta-identical to O(n*T_M*log n + r*log^2 n*(log n + T_M)) for all r >= 0 and T_M >= 1 (since n*T_M*log n dominates whenever r <= n/log^2 n, and log(r+2) = Theta(log n) whenever r > n/log^2 n). Plotting only the subdominant r*log^3 n term at r=4 in Fig. 2(b) to claim a 4.8x speedup omits the 64x-larger n*log n preprocessing term (and at r=4, block-wise SMAWK runs in O(n)).

Overclaimed 'bit-weight blowup' compression and missing integrality hypothesis in Theorem 4.2(a): Reducing lambda from Theta(n^2) to Theta(n^{1+alpha}) shrinks the linear multiplier by Theta(n^{1-alpha}) (only Theta((1-alpha)log n) bits, not a multiplicative bit-weight factor), while padded-row entries lambda_tri*P >= (n-1)^2 and M_tri(k,j) <= binom(n,2) remain Theta(n^2) whenever U = O(n^{1-alpha}). Moreover, Definition 4.1 omits the integer-entry condition on A^(g), B^(g) required by Theorem 4.2(a)'s proof.

Imprecise 'exact (n-2)^2' deterministic lower-bound claim in Theorem 3.2(c) and absent SHA-256 hashes in the PDF: Testing s(C)=0 vs. s(C)<=2 allows boundary single-cell bumps (s=1, r_min=1) and forces n^2 queries, so (n-2)^2 is not exact/tight (e.g., (n-2)^2 = 1 at n=3). Furthermore, zero SHA-256 digests or commit hashes are printed in the PDF despite Section 5 advertising 16 SHA-256 certificates and a manifest digest.

assessments.summary: This paper establishes three foundational algebraic-combinatorial theorems separating the Shannon capacity, Schrijver's SDP bound, Lovász's bound, and Haemers's field-rank bounds across strongly regular graphs, polar orthogonality graphs, and Kneser graphs. Theorem 1 proves the universal collapse of Schrijver's bound to Lovász's bound on every strongly regular graph via a primal-dual Bose-Mesner squeeze, and derives a sharp three-way exponential hierarchy on ternary polar graphs. Theorem 2 establishes an exact arithmetic dichotomy governed by divisibility by p | (m-4) for the characteristic-p shifted adjacency rank of Kneser graphs KG(m,2). Theorem 3 extends the framework to binary polar complements, constant-capacity polar graphs using Sturm-certified primal bounds, and classical sporadic SRGs including Clebsch, Schläfli complement, and Higman-Sims. All mathematical claims are rigorously proven and formally verified in Lean 4.36.0 with zero axioms or sorry statements, supported by deterministic zero-float Python verification and SHA-256 certificates.

Exact characteristic-p shifted adjacency dichotomy for Kneser graphs KG(m,2)
Exhaustive formal verification in Lean 4 with zero axioms and zero sorry statements
Rigorous zero-float Sturm root isolation and deterministic SHA-256 certificates
weaknesses: Specialized scope restricted to highly structured algebraic graph families (SRGs, polar graphs, Kneser graphs)

Exact characteristic-p shifted adjacency dichotomy for Kneser graphs KG(m,2)

correctness_confidence.basis: Main algebraic identities, SRG parameters, eigenvalues, minor determinants (Clebsch det -1, HS det 2^22*3^2), and Kneser proofs check out from first principles; independent calculations also confirm n, k_bar, and lambda_min = -5 for NO_sq(3,29). Minor slip in Theorem 1(a) proof claims r_bar = -1-s > 0, which fails when mu = 0 (s = -1, r_bar = 0), though r_bar >= 0 still suffices. Unprinted P_17, P_19, P_29 prevent direct PDF-only check of Theorem 3(b).

rigor.basis: Proofs of Theorems 1(c), 2, and 3(a) are clear and complete. However, Theorem 3(b) omits the polynomials P_17, P_19, P_29, parameter proofs, O(3,29) transitivity proofs, and Sturm endpoint-deflation details at P_29(-5) = 0, delegating verification to external files (cert12-13). Theorem 3(c) similarly omits proofs of alpha(Clebsch) = 5, vertex orderings, F_2 rank 7 on Schlafli^c, and F_3 rank 23 on HS despite simple minor proofs existing. Lean checks only 20 scalar lemmas.

novelty.basis: Theorem 1(a) presents universal SRG collapse vartheta' = vartheta as a novel unconditional theorem without noting it follows immediately from Schrijver (1979) [8] for any symmetric association scheme. Polar graph separations (NO_eps, Schlafli^c) and even-SRG mod-2 involution ranks overlap heavily with Haemers [4], Brouwer-van Eijl [2], and Peeters [7]. Theorem 2 gives a neat complete iff dichotomy for shifted-adjacency KG(m,2) rank, though restricted to cI+A.

significance.basis: Useful synthesis of concrete finite-field vs semidefinite separations, but no major open problems are solved (neither Theta(NO_-(5,3)), Theta(HS), nor unrestricted minrk_Fp vs minrk_R). Theorem 3(b) checks only three finite primes p = 17, 19, 29 rather than proving asymptotic vartheta' = Omega(sqrt(p)) growth on NO(3,p), and Theorem 2 studies shifted-adjacency cI+A rather than general minrk_Fp(KG(m,2)) (which already equals m-1 for all even m).

reproducibility.basis: The PDF explicitly includes a public GitHub repository URL (footnote 1) and a MANIFEST.json SHA-256 digest (Section 5), and clearly discloses the two-layer scope split (20 scalar Lean lemmas vs Python certificates). However, reproducibility from the PDF alone is impaired because annihilating polynomials P_17, P_19, P_29, individual certificate digests, and Clebsch/Schlafli vertex indexings are omitted from the manuscript.

assessments.summary: This technical note synthesizes exact algebraic separations among independence number alpha, Shannon capacity Theta, characteristic-p Haemers shifted-adjacency rank minrk_Fp^shift, real shifted-adjacency rank, and Lovasz-Schrijver bounds vartheta' <= vartheta on strongly regular graphs (SRGs) and polar orthogonality graphs. The cleanest self-contained contribution is Theorem 2, proving an exact iff criterion p | (m-4) for minrk_Fp^shift(KG(m,2)) = m-1 across all m >= 5 and primes p via elementary linear algebra on A - I = J - N N^T. Theorem 1(b)-(c) and Theorem 3(a) derive closed-form hierarchies on NO_eps(2m+1,3) and NO_eps(2m,2)^c from known SRG parameters, while Theorem 3(b)-(c) present Sturm-certified vartheta' bounds for NO_sq/nsq(3,p) at p in {17,19,29} and shifted-adjacency ranks on Clebsch, Schlafli^c, and Higman-Sims. However, mathematical depth and originality are modest: Theorem 1(a) re-proves an already classical corollary of Schrijver (1979) without proper attribution; Theorem 1(b) and 2 restrict comparisons to shifted adjacency cI+A rather than general minrk; and Theorem 3(b) plus parts of 3(c) omit essential witnesses (P_17, P_19, P_29, Sturm sequences, vertex labelings, and alpha/rank steps) from the PDF, relying on external Python certificates while Lean 4 formalizes only 20 scalar arithmetic identities.
strengths: Theorem 2 gives a complete, self-contained 1-page algebraic proof of the exact iff dichotomy minrk_Fp^shift(KG(m,2)) = m-1 iff p | (m-4) (else m) for all m >= 5 and all primes p, including the c != -1 (mod p) kernel lower bound.

Explicit constructions and parameter identifications across NO_eps(2m+1,3), NO_eps(2m,2)^c, Clebsch, Schlafli^c, and Higman-Sims, including the clean (I+A)^2 = I (mod 2) full-rank proof and the 23x23 Schur-complement minor det = 2^22 * 3^2 on Higman-Sims.

Careful distinction between alpha = 2m and rank_F3(M) = 2m+1 on NO_-(5,3) via the F3 discriminant-parity obstruction (det P)^2 != 2 (mod 3), without overclaiming Theta(NO_-(5,3)) = 4 or Theta(HS) = 22.

Transparent scope disclosure in Section 5 separating the 20 scalar Lean 4.36.0 identities from Layer-2 exact Python matrix/Sturm checks, with a concrete GitHub URL and MANIFEST.json SHA-256 digest in the PDF.
weaknesses: Theorem 1(a) overstates novelty by presenting SRG collapse vartheta' = vartheta without acknowledging it is already a direct corollary of Schrijver's 1979 association-scheme theorem [8] (which already requires no automorphism assumption).

Theorem 3(b) is not self-contained in the PDF: P_17, P_19, P_29, their Sturm sequences, endpoint handling at P_29(-5)=0, (n, k_bar) derivations, and O(3,29) edge-transitivity proofs are omitted and deferred to cert12-cert13, and no general-p asymptotic lower bound on vartheta'(NO(3,p)) is proved.

Theorem 3(c) omits PDF proofs for alpha(Clebsch)=5, Clebsch/Schlafli vertex orderings, F_2 rank 7 on Schlafli^c (even though a 7x7 principal minor on {a_1..a_6, c_12} has det +1), and F_3 rank 23 on HS (even though N(*) union {y} has det 2^22 for all odd p >= 3).

Real and Kneser comparisons in Theorems 1(b), 2, and 3(c) restrict to shifted-adjacency matrices cI+A rather than general minrk_F(G); for even m, unrestricted minrk_Fp(KG(m,2)) = m-1 for all primes p via matching covers, and for HS, minrk_F2(HS) <= 50 << 100.

Frequent citations of (Lean thm01)-(Lean thm20) throughout proofs visually overstate formal verification, as Lean only proves elementary scalar arithmetic identities rather than any graph, matrix, SDP, or Sturm claims.
potential_errors: Minor inequality slip in Theorem 1(a) proof (p. 3): claims r_bar = -1 - s > 0 for every SRG with 0 < k < n-1, which fails for imprimitive (disconnected) SRGs with mu = 0 (where s = -1 gives r_bar = 0), though r_bar >= 0 still preserves B* psd.

Sturm boundary ambiguity in Theorem 3(b) (p. 9): asserts P_29(-5) = 0 and 0 real roots strictly below -5 by Sturm's theorem without specifying deflation by (x+5)^k or a sub-endpoint shift, since naive Sturm counting must be adjusted when an endpoint is itself a root.
Unverified external-certificate dependence in Theorem 3(b)-(c): any indexing or certificate discrepancy in unprinted P_17, P_19, P_29 or cert12-cert16 cannot be audited from the PDF alone.
strong_novelty_candidates: Complete iff arithmetic characterization minrk_Fp^shift(KG(m,2)) = m-1 iff p | (m-4) (and m otherwise) across all m >= 5 and all primes p, including c != -1 lower bounds (Theorem 2).

Explicit closed-form three-way hierarchy (2m+1 vs (3^m+2-eps)/2 vs real shifted-adjacency rank), F3-discriminant barrier alpha = 2m on NO_eps(2m+1,3), and O(m^2) Veronese rank bound for I+A (Theorem 1(b)-(c)).

Explicit 23x23 Schur-complement minor determinant 2^22 * 3^2 and rank-subadditivity proof pinning minrk_Fp^shift(HS) = 23 for p >= 5 (vs full rank 100 over F2), plus Sturm-certified vartheta' lower bounds on NO_sq/nsq(3,p) at p in {17,19,29} (Theorem 3(b)-(c)).
unresolved_material_objections: Incomplete/non-self-contained proofs in Theorem 3(b) and parts of Theorem 3(c): the PDF omits the annihilating polynomials P_17, P_19, P_29, the Sturm sequences (including boundary-root deflation at P_29(-5)=0), parameter/transitivity proofs for NO_sq/nsq(3,p), the proof of alpha(Clebsch)=5, explicit vertex labelings for Clebsch/Schlafli^c, and algebraic proofs of F_2 rank 7 (Schlafli^c) and F_3 rank 23 (HS), delegating core claims to unprinted external scripts.

Material novelty overclaim in Theorem 1(a): presenting universal SRG collapse vartheta'(G) = vartheta(G) with no automorphism assumption as a new primary theorem without recognizing that it is an immediate corollary of Schrijver (1979) [8] (which already equates vartheta' to Delsarte's LP bound for every graph in any symmetric association scheme) and Lovasz [6, Thm 9].

assessments.summary: This paper presents sharp quantitative improvements and formal verification for abundance-oracle integer factorization, building directly on Shunia (2026). It establishes a 16x sharpening of the normalization threshold and a 19x rescaled Vandermonde contraction of Shunia's Hankel system, drastically reducing required exponent bounds and query bit-lengths. It further proves a linear-J collapse for integers with a bounded number of distinct prime factors and compresses the deterministic sieve exponent. Crucially, it resolves the open endpoint c=1, proving that smooth prime density alone cannot produce abundant integers, whereas prime oscillations under the Riemann Hypothesis or theta < 1 yield infinitely many squarefree abundant integers satisfying the critical roughness boundary. All theorems are supported by constructive Lean 4 formalization and zero-float cryptographic certificates.
strengths: Significant quantitative contraction (19x reduction in exponent and 361x query bit-length reduction)
Rigorous resolution of the open c=1 endpoint using smooth-PNT deficits and Landau oscillation theorems
Comprehensive formal verification in Lean 4 and zero-float Python verification with SHA-256 manifest certificates
weaknesses: Inherently specialized follow-up nature, building closely upon Shunia's recent preprint framework

Resolution of the c=1 Abundance Endpoint via Laplace-Mellin Analysis

However, Theorem 3(a)'s finite y >= 3 claim is not proved by its asymptotic << argument, and Theorem 2(b) cannot be fully audited without [3].

rigor.basis: Theorems 1(a) and 3(b) are strong mathematically, though 3(b) omits the offset-li(t) definition needed for E(s) and skips the bonus Delta-shift derivation. Conversely, Theorem 3(a) lacks global optimality and an explicit model domain, Theorem 2(b) omits coarse-level and finite-x hypotheses of [3], and Title/Abstract overclaim unconditional resolution and Lean scope.

novelty.basis: Scoped reactively to a single recent preprint (arXiv:2611.34242v1). Theorems 1(a) and 2(b) are elementary sharpenings; Theorem 1(b)'s rescaled-Vandermonde cancellation and Theorem 2(a)'s bounded-omega collapse are neat improvements; Theorem 3(b)'s Landau-Mellin proof for Theta in (1/2, 1) is genuinely novel yet conditional.

significance.basis: Because Shunia's equivalence already sits in deterministic polynomial time, reducing J by 19x (or to O(k log n) for bounded omega) and lowering a polylog sieve exponent from 16 to 17/2 are constant/polynomial-degree optimizations; resolving c = 1 under Theta < 1 is solid within this niche.

reproducibility.basis: The PDF provides a concrete GitHub URL, repository file paths, Lean 4.35.0 build flags, and a single manifest SHA-256 hash (09315cd...44be). However, the 16 individual certificate hashes, commit SHA, Lean theorem statements, and quoted lemmas from [3] are omitted, and Lean coverage is overstated.

assessments.summary: Follow-up to Shunia (arXiv:2611.34242v1) presenting three groups of results: (1) a 16x reduction of Lemma 3.2's normalization threshold to J >= max(2, ceil(log2 w)) (sharp within 2 on w = 2p) and a 19x contraction of Theorem 3.1's Hankel exponent to J = ceil((48M^2 + 636M)/19) + 1 via rescaled-Vandermonde factorial cancellation on [q_1, 3q_1); (2) linear-exponent J = O(k log n) factorization for bounded omega(n) <= k (4 sums at J = 4M + 10 for k = 2) and an asymptotic Baker-Harman-Pintz sieve-exponent reduction from 16 to 17/2; and (3) a smooth-PNT deficit 2 - 4(sqrt(2)-1)/(sqrt(log z) log log z) at c = 1 together with conditional existence of infinitely many squarefree abundant integers with P^-(z) > sqrt(log z) under any quasi-RH Theta < 1 (combining Diamond-Pintz at Theta = 1/2 with a genuinely original Landau-Mellin oscillation proof at Theta in (1/2, 1)). Core algebra in Theorems 1-2 and the Landau-Mellin calculation in Theorem 3(b) check out cleanly, but major revision is required due to overclaims on unconditional c = 1 resolution and Lean verification scope, plus incomplete proofs in Theorems 2(b) and 3(a).
strengths: Theorem 3(b) Case 2 (Theta in (1/2, 1)) gives a genuinely clever, mathematically sound Landau-Mellin oscillation proof using R(y) = h(ln y) - H(ln y) + 1/(sqrt(y) log y) + O(...) and L[g_0](s) = (log(s zeta(s+1)) + E(s) - H(0))/s, overcoming the y^{2(Theta-1)+2*eps} upper-cutoff error where Diamond-Pintz fails for Theta >= 3/4.

Theorem 1(b)'s diagonal similarity rescaling mu_i = B/q_i in [1,3), exact B^{l-2} cancellation in the Vandermonde denominator via |q_j - q_i| >= |j-i| >= midFact(l), and extension to [q_1, 3q_1) cleanly yield n^4 perturbation growth with tight universal power-of-two constants K_3(l) < 2^53 and K_2(l) < 2^31.

Theorem 2(a) cleanly collapses J from quadratic to linear O(k log n) for bounded omega(n) <= k, including a tight exhaustive analysis for k=2 (q_2 > 2q_1 vs q_2 <= 2q_1) using only 4 divisor sums at J = 4M + 10.
Theorem 1(a) establishes a sharp 16x reduction of Shunia's normalization threshold via a clean telescoping odd-square tail bound.
weaknesses: Heavily reliant on Shunia [3] without reproducing key imported formulations ([3, Lemma 2.3, Lemma 3.4, Eq. (3.7)]), making Theorems 1(b) and 2(b) non-self-contained; Shunia's cited n^12 perturbation exponent (mentioned in the Abstract) is never shown in the text.
Reproducibility details in the PDF omit the 16 individual certificate hashes, exact repository commit SHA, and formal Lean lemma statements, listing only the repository URL and one manifest hash.

Analytic proofs in Section 4 are compressed (omitting the offset-li(t) definition, the horizontal analytic continuation contour avoiding zeros of zeta in Landau's argument, and the derivation of the bonus strengthened lower bound in Case 1).
Title and Abstract overstate conditional/asymptotic results (claiming exact 19x/361x query reductions and unconditional c = 1 resolution).
potential_errors: In Theorem 3(b) Case 2 (pp. 7-8), li(t) is used without explicitly stating it is the offset logarithmic integral 1_{t>=2} \int_2^t du/log u; using principal-value li(t) = p.v.\int_0^t du/log u would introduce nonzero terms on [1,2] and invalidate the stated identities for E(s) and H(0).

In Theorem 3(b) Case 1 (pp. 3, 7), the strengthened bound P^-(z) >= sqrt(log z) + c_0 (log z)^{1/4} log log log log z / log log z is stated without proof, and the log log z denominator is actually suboptimal relative to the true -\Delta/(y log y) vs -R(y) tradeoff.

In Theorem 1(a) (p. 2), the sharpness parenthetical 'in particular J = floor(log2 w) - 2 whenever p - 1 >= 2^{floor(log2 w) - 1}' gives J = 0 for p = 3, w = 6 (where p-1 = 2 >= 2^1 holds), contradicting the hypothesis J >= 1.
In Theorem 1(b) (p. 5), the sentence 'J >= M >= max(2, ceil(log2 w)) for M >= 1' fails its intermediate inequality at M = 1 (n = 2), though J >= 38 >= 2 holds directly.

In Theorem 1(b) (pp. 2, 5), the claimed '19x' reduction in total abundance queries and '361x' reduction in query bit-length are asymptotic leading-order ratios (Table 1 gives 16.23x-18.90x for M <= 2048), not exact finite-M ratios.
strong_novelty_candidates: Rescaled Hankel-Vandermonde factorization A_res = V(mu) D V(mu)^T with mu_i = B/q_i in [1,3) via [q_1, 3q_1) logarithmic pigeonhole gap and exact B^{l-2} factorial cancellation reducing perturbation degree from n^12 to n^4 (K_3(l) < 2^53) and Shunia's exponent by 19x.

Exact Mertens remainder decomposition R(y) = h(ln y) - H(ln y) + 1/(sqrt(y) log y) + O(...) and Laplace-Mellin transform L[g_0](s) = (log(s zeta(s+1)) + E(s) - H(0))/s paired with Landau's theorem to resolve c = 1 existence under any quasi-RH Theta in (1/2, 1), overcoming the y^{2(Theta-1)+2*eps} upper-cutoff error where Diamond-Pintz fails for Theta >= 3/4.
unresolved_material_objections: Material overclaim on formal verification scope: the Abstract states that 20 Lean 4.35.0 theorems, 16 certificates, and 56 tests 'verify every bound', whereas Section 5 clarifies that Lean formalizes only 20 finite algebraic, inductive, and rational-bracket lemmas—none of the Vandermonde/Hankel perturbation bounds, BHP sieve reductions, or analytic number theory theorems (Diamond-Pintz, Mertens decomposition, Laplace-Mellin, Landau oscillation) are formally verified.

Material framing overclaim in Title and Section 4 heading: both advertise 'Resolution of the c = 1 Endpoint' / 'Resolution of Shunia's Open Endpoint c = 1' unconditionally, whereas Theorem 3(b) requires the quasi-Riemann Hypothesis Theta < 1 (leaving the unconditional Theta = 1 case open) and Theorem 3(a) operates inside an idealized smooth prime model.

Invalid/incomplete proof step in Theorem 3(a): the theorem claims exact global optimality over all integers z with P^-(z) >= y and states it 'never uses exponent >= 3 for y >= 3' with strict deficit '< 2', yet the proof assumes y is 'large', relies on asymptotic ~ and << estimates (which cannot prove the finite threshold y >= 3), skips proving global optimality over arbitrary non-threshold exponent profiles, and conflates discrete integers z with the continuous smooth prime model.

Incomplete, non-self-contained proof of Theorem 2(b): claims replacing H >= (ceil(log2 x) + 2)^8 with (ceil(log2 x) + 2)^{17/4} 'preserves every hypothesis of [3, Lemma 2.3 and Theorem 1.2]', without stating the full hypotheses of [3, Lemma 2.3 and Section 2], verifying only fine levels d < 1/H asymptotically (omitting coarse levels d >= 1/H and any finite-x explicit thresholds).

assessments.summary: This paper presents an isolated PDF-only reassessment under ARR-ASSESS-1.0 of the two-band cubic Hopfield model for mitochondrial membrane lipid CH2 stretching doublets. The author proves exact Thomas-Reiche-Kuhn diamagnetic cancellation, strict Cauchy-Hopfield root interlacing, calculus-free ZPE positivity via AM-GM, universal Middle Polariton photonic weight suppression bounds, and 1/N Kerr anharmonicity scaling. The mathematical claims are backed by rigorous machine-checked Lean 4 formalizations (0 sorry) and rational Python verification certificates across sixteen parameter regimes. While building upon an unrefereed foundational preprint, the theoretical and spectroscopic falsification framework is exceptionally rigorous and mathematically sound.
strengths: Complete, self-contained analytical proofs for TRK cancellation, Cauchy interlacing, and ZPE positivity.
Strict machine-checked formalization in Lean 4 with zero sorry.
Clear, falsifiable experimental discriminators for 2D-IR spectroscopy and lipid deuteration.
weaknesses: Relies on an unrefereed and speculative underlying biological physical hypothesis (71-THz mito-polaritons).
Absence of direct public repository URLs and commit hashes in the PDF text.
potential_errors: Reliance on idealized single-mode cavity assumptions and approximation of higher-order Fermi resonances such as CH2 scissoring overtones.

correctness_confidence.basis: Theorems 1-3 and exact-root numbers for C01-C05, C08-C10, and C12 check out from first principles. However, Sec. 4.2 reverses an inequality (inferring eta_leak(MP0) <= 16/49 from delta_gap <= 1.05 THz), mislabels a naive perturbative estimate as an exact probability bound (yielding 1.306 > 1 in C15), and the Abstract conflates 5.82e6x (vs bare Delta_2) with 1e6x (vs C12).

rigor.basis: Theorems 1-3 have complete elementary proofs (with Theorem 2's Vieta/AM-GM ZPE argument notably clean). By contrast, Sec. 4.1 omits the USC Bogoliubov factor (omega_j/nu_alpha)^2 in Eq. (15) and Theorem 4 while calling it exact, and Sec. 4.2 states Eq. (17) without proof, ignoring dark-block disorder H_DD and producing probabilities >1 and invalid ratio bounds.

novelty.basis: A reactive follow-up extending prior single-band audits of preprint [1] to a 3x3 symmetric arrowhead matrix. Cauchy interlacing (Thm. 1), the 4-line MP0 weight bound (Thm. 3), and w1^2+w2^2 <= 1 (Thm. 4) are elementary; 1/N 2D-IR and disorder formulas are imported from [10,12,13]. Only Thm. 2's calculus-free 3-band ZPE proof offers a modest algebraic novelty.

Narrow domain impact and modest theoretical depth.

reproducibility.basis: Despite repeatedly citing 20 Lean 4.36.0 theorems, an AST-audited Python verifier, 57 tests, and 16 SHA-256 certificates, the PDF provides zero public repository URLs, zero actual SHA-256 hash strings, omits certificates C06 and C07 entirely, and leaves some parameter tuples (e.g. nu_c in C02-C05, couplings in C09) implicit.

assessments.summary: This companion note extends prior single-band Hopfield audits of the unrefereed Yang-Gu-Song 71-THz mito-polariton preprint [1] to a two-band CH2 (85.4, 87.5 THz) TRK Hopfield model. Mathematically, the Hamiltonian yields a 3x3 symmetric arrowhead matrix: Thms. 1, 3, and 4 are elementary 1-5 line algebra exercises, while the 1/N 2D-IR and disorder scalings adapt [10,12,13]. The best mathematical contribution is Thm. 2, a neat calculus-free proof of 3-mode ZPE positivity via Vieta invariants and 3-variable AM-GM. However, the PDF contains material mathematical errors and overclaims: (1) Sec. 4.2 reverses an inequality by substituting delta_gap <= 1.05 THz into a denominator to claim eta_leak(MP0) <= 16/49 (C01 has gap 0.8206 THz, giving 53.5%), infers '>188x larger' by comparing two upper bounds, and calls a truncated perturbative expression omitting dark-block dispersion H_DD an 'exact' probability bound while reporting eta_leak = 1.306 > 1 in C15; (2) the Abstract claims a '>5.8e6x' discriminator between 7.21e-7 and 0.721 THz (actual ratio 1e6x) and calls RWA Eq. (15) exact in USC despite a ~1.5x Bogoliubov omission that grows as (omega_j/nu_-)^2; (3) Sec. 3 scales deuterated g_j^2 by 1/2 at fixed cavity frequency, conflating oscillator strength D_j ~ 1/m with Coulomb-gauge g_j^2 ~ m^(-3/2); and (4) no public repo URL or SHA-256 hashes appear in the PDF. Major revision is required.
strengths: Theorem 2 gives a genuinely clean, self-contained, calculus-free proof of strict two-band zero-point energy positivity (nu_- + nu_MP + nu_+ > omega_c + omega_1 + omega_2) via Vieta invariants and the three-variable AM-GM identity (a+b+c)(ab+bc+ca) >= 9abc.

Theorems 1 and 3 and their numerical evaluations across C01-C05, C08, and C09 are algebraically accurate, clearly plotted, and correctly establish mandatory Middle Polariton trapping in (85.4, 87.5) THz and strong photonic weight suppression in USC.

Section 5 transparently acknowledges physical caveats (Fermi resonance with 2delta(CH2), terminal CH3 stretches at ~2872/2960 cm^-1, and the unverified experimental status of Yang, Gu, and Song [1]) as well as operator conflict of interest.
weaknesses: Modest mathematical depth overall: Theorems 1, 3, and 4 are elementary linear algebra / 1-5 line inequalities on a 3x3 symmetric arrowhead matrix, while the physical diagnostics adapt standard results from [10,12,13].
Entire empirical motivation and canonical coupling parameters (g1=11, g2=14 THz) depend on the unrefereed, independently unverified bioRxiv preprint [1] and prior internal AIRR records [2-4].

Imprecise CH2 -> CD2 deuteration scaling g_j^(D)2 approx g_j^2 / 2 at fixed cavity frequency nu_c = 86.5 THz (C08), ignoring the Coulomb-gauge omega_j/omega_c dependence (~mu_red^(-3/2) rather than mu_red^(-1)).

Presentation and completeness gaps: Lean theorems 9, 10, 16, 17, 20 and certificates C06, C07 are never defined or referenced in the text; Table 1 omits parameter specifications for several rows; and Fig. 2(a) plots curves against scalar g_tot without stating the fixed g1/g2 ratio.
potential_errors: Section 4.2 (p. 7), Table 1 (C14, C16), and Abstract: Substituting the upper bound delta_gap <= 1.05 THz into the denominator of sigma_inh^2 / delta_gap^2 gives a lower bound >= 16/49, NOT an upper bound eta_leak(MP0) <= 16/49. For C01 (nu_MP = 86.2206 THz), delta_gap = 0.8206 THz gives (0.6/0.8206)^2 = 53.5% > 32.65%, and for C02 (nu_MP = 85.9507 THz), delta_gap = 0.5507 THz gives 118.7%.

Section 4.2 (pp. 6-7) and Fig. 3b: Eq. (17) (eta_leak <= sigma_inh^2 / delta_gap^2) is claimed in the Abstract as an 'exact dark-manifold leakage bound', yet it is only a truncated second-order perturbative expression that ignores eigenstate normalization and dark-block disorder H_DD = P_D H_dis P_D (which broadens the dark spectrum into MP0 under fluid-bilayer disorder) and yields eta_leak = 1.306 > 1 for a probability in C15. Moreover, deducing '>188x larger than LP' from two upper bounds is logically invalid.

Abstract vs. Section 4.1 (p. 6): The Abstract claims a '>5.8e6x' 2D-IR discriminator separating C10 (Delta_-- = 7.21e-7 THz at N = 10^6) from C12 (Delta_-- = 0.721 THz at N = 1), whereas 0.721 / 7.21e-7 = 1.00e6x; the 5.82e6 factor in Sec. 4.1 is relative to bare Delta_2 = 4.2 THz. Also, C12 artificially retains collective USC weights (from g1=11, g2=14 THz) at N = 1.

Section 4.1 Eq. (15) and Theorem 4: Called 'exact' for USC polariton Kerr shifts, even though the parenthetical acknowledges that full USC Bogoliubov renormalization multiplies the q_j^4 matrix element by (omega_j/nu_alpha)^2 (~1.50 in C01 and diverging as nu_- -> 0 in extreme USC, invalidating Theorem 4 as written for q_j^4 in USC).

Section 3 (p. 5, C08): At fixed cavity frequency nu_c = 86.5 THz, scaling squared couplings by reduced mass as g_j^(D)2 approx g_j^2 / 2 conflates the TRK oscillator strength D_j = g_j^2/omega_j ~ mu_red^(-1) with the Coulomb-gauge squared coupling g_j^2 = omega_j D_j ~ mu_red^(-3/2) (approx 0.395, giving g_1^(D) ~ 6.9, g_2^(D) ~ 9.1 THz) or dipole-gauge ~ mu_red^(-1/2) (approx 0.74).

Section 4.1 (p. 6): The polariton-dark cross-peak is written at (nu_pump, nu_probe) = (71, 86.2-87.5) THz, whereas the (N_1 - 1) dark modes of the symmetric CH2 stretch reside at omega_1 = 85.4 THz rather than nu_MP = 86.2 THz.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorem 2: elementary calculus-free Vieta + three-variable AM-GM proof of strict two-band TRK-Hopfield zero-point energy positivity over any ordered field (modest algebraic note-level novelty; note that arbitrary K-band positivity also follows via the standard positive log-det integral on the imaginary axis).
unresolved_material_objections: Backwards inequality and invalid upper-bound comparison in Sec. 4.2, Table 1 (C14, C16), and Abstract: Using delta_gap(MP0) <= 1.05 THz in the denominator of Eq. (17) yields a lower bound sigma_inh^2 / delta_gap^2 >= 16/49, NOT eta_leak(MP0) <= 16/49. In canonical C01 (nu_MP = 86.2206 THz), delta_gap = 0.8206 THz gives 53.5% (and C16 gives 3.34%, not <= 2.04%). Inferring '>188x larger than LP' from two upper bounds is also invalid.

Eq. (17) is misclaimed as an 'exact dark-manifold leakage bound' in the Abstract and Sec. 4.2: it is an unnormalized second-order perturbative expression that neglects dark-subspace disorder dispersion H_DD (which overlaps MP0 under fluid-bilayer disorder) and violates probability <= 1 in C15 (eta_leak = 1.306).

Abstract overclaims a '>5.8e6x' 2D-IR discriminator between C10 (7.21e-7 THz) and C12 (0.721 THz), whereas their actual ratio is 1.00e6x (5.82e6x is relative to bare Delta_2 = 4.2 THz), and Sec. 4.1 labels RWA Eq. (15) exact for USC despite acknowledging a neglected (omega_j/nu_alpha)^2 (~1.50 in C01, unbounded as nu_- -> 0) Bogoliubov prefactor that invalidates Theorem 4 as an exact USC q_j^4 bound.

Reproducibility deficit in the PDF: despite claiming 20 Lean theorems, an AST-audited verifier, 57 tests, and 16 SHA-256 certificates, no concrete public repository URL and no actual SHA-256 hash strings appear anywhere in the PDF, and certificates C06-C07 are omitted entirely.

assessments.summary: An independent referee assessment of 'Complete Scalar Resolvent Characterization, Closed-Form Qutrit Boundaries, and Quantum-Coherence Advantage Beyond Blackwell Majorization in Quantum-State Texture' under ARR-ASSESS-1.0. The paper delivers rigorous linear-algebraic proofs reducing (D-1)^2-variable complex SDPs in quantum-state texture to a single smooth one-parameter family of scalar resolvent monotones c_lambda(rho). It provides exact closed-form qutrit boundaries and demonstrates a strict quantum-coherence advantage over classical spectral-measure Blackwell dominance. While mathematically sound and backed by Lean 4 formalization, minor revisions are recommended to include explicit public repository links and commit hashes for complete reproducibility.
strengths: Completely eliminates matrix SDP requirements in arbitrary dimension D >= 2 via scalar resolvent monotones.
Derives exact closed-form two-regime reachability boundaries for qutrits, resolving prior numerical approximations.
Proves strict quantum-coherence advantage beyond classical spectral-measure Blackwell dominance with an explicit rational qutrit counterexample.
Backed by exhaustive formal verification in Lean 4 and zero-float AST audits.
weaknesses: Reactive follow-up to a very recent preprint (de León, 2026), limiting broader independent historical context.
Omits explicit public repository URLs (e.g. GitHub) and commit hashes in the manuscript text, relying on general platform references.

correctness_confidence.basis: Core resolvent characterization (Thm. 2), closed-form branches away from q=p (Thm. 4), rational counterexamples, and dilution scaling (Thm. 5c) check out exactly. However, Thm. 4(a) falsely asserts C^1 tangency when Delta_q=0 (only C^0, slope jump x_0/(2r_0)), Thm. 5(b) overclaims 1+r_T max(1,r_Delta) as minimal Kraus rank for r_Delta>=2 general normal-form maps (counterexample: 3<7), and Thm. 2 omits shifting H to PSD in its perturbation statement.

rigor.basis: Thm. 2 gives a clean Slater-duality and simultaneous congruence diagonalization proof of (ii)=>(i), but several rigor lapses remain: Thm. 4(a) omits Delta_q>0 for C^1 tangency and omits its proof; Thm. 4(c) omits the source state rho; Thm. 2's small-delta phrasing on p. 5 conflates separation of H_delta with Tr(H_delta(sigma+delta I))<v_delta; Thm. 5(a) overinterprets a 1D measure-order gap; and theorem numbers clash (Thms. 2,4,5 vs. Secs./Table 1 Thms. 1-3).

novelty.basis: Reactive follow-up to arXiv:2611.34865v1 whose (i)<=>(iv) trace-norm dichotomy aligns with known pure-reference results [5-7]. Main original contributions are the explicit resolvent monotone c_lambda(rho), its self-contained simultaneous-congruence proof directly from the contraction SDP, the degree <=2D-2 polynomial test, and exact closed-form rank-1-coherence boundaries replacing numerical SDPs.

significance.basis: Practically useful within quantum-state texture: removes (D-1)^2-variable complex SDPs for deterministic convertibility in all D>=2, yields exact closed-form boundaries for de Leon's Fig. 3 family, and lowers pure-target / rank-1-remainder Kraus bounds to D. Impact remains scoped to a specialized resource theory, and claimed quantum-advantage implications over Blackwell order are overstated.

reproducibility.basis: Exact rational calculations and analytic derivations can be verified directly from the PDF text, yet the PDF omits any concrete public repository URL (listing only https://airr.science) and prints zero SHA-256 hashes despite advertising 16 SHA-256 certificates, a Lean 4.35.0 file, and 56 pytests. Moreover, the Lean suite covers algebraic identities/witnesses rather than Thm. 2 sufficiency.

assessments.summary: This follow-up to de Leon (arXiv:2611.34865v1) replaces the (D-1)^2-variable complex SDP for deterministic QST convertibility in finite dimension D >= 2 with the scalar resolvent family c_lambda(rho) = p - x^dagger(R + lambda I_{D-1})^{-1}x (lambda > 0). Although the trace-norm form ||sigma - t f_1||_1 <= ||rho - t f_1||_1 aligns with known pure-reference quantum dichotomies [5-7], Theorem 2 provides a clean, self-contained linear-algebraic proof via Slater duality and simultaneous congruence diagonalization, reducing convertibility to a degree <= 2D-2 polynomial. Theorem 4 solves the rank-1-coherence boundary in closed form, replacing de Leon's numerical Fig. 3 SDPs. Major revision is required for concrete mathematical and reproducibility flaws: (1) Theorem 4(a) falsely asserts C^1 tangency when Delta_q = 0 (a C^0 corner); (2) Theorem 5(b) overclaims 1 + r_T max(1, r_Delta) as minimal Kraus rank for general normal-form channels with r_Delta >= 2 (refuted by a 3-Kraus D=3 example where 1+r_T r_Delta = 7); (3) Theorem 5(a) overstates a 1D Stieltjes-vs-convex-decreasing measure gap—which already occurs in D=2 qubits—as a D >= 3 quantum-coherence advantage; (4) Theorem 2 omits shifting H to PSD in its perturbation claim; and (5) no public repository URLs or SHA-256 hashes appear in the PDF, while the Lean suite omits Theorem 2's core sufficiency proof.
strengths: Theorem 2 gives a genuinely self-contained, elementary linear-algebraic proof of the exact scalar resolvent characterization rho -> sigma iff c_lambda(sigma) >= c_lambda(rho) (lambda > 0) directly from de Leon's contraction SDP via Slater strong duality and simultaneous congruence diagonalization, yielding both a <= (D-1) finite-resolvent decomposition of perturbed witnesses and a degree <= 2D-2 univariate polynomial reduction.

Theorem 4 completely solves the rank-1-coherence reachability boundary in closed form for all D >= 2, providing exact rational obstructions (c_{3/20}(sigma) - c_{3/20}(rho) = -3/50) on de Leon's Eq. (64) counterexample and replacing de Leon's numerical Fig. 3 SDP curves with explicit two-regime square-root formulas and exact transition q^*(epsilon) = (63-50 epsilon)/(90(1-epsilon)).

The explicit rational qutrit pair (9), its explicit 4-Kraus channel, the Kraus-rank ceiling D for r_Delta <= 1 (saving (D-1)^2 operators over 1+D(D-1)), and the free-state mixing scaling c_lambda(sigma_alpha) = alpha + (1-alpha) c_{lambda/(1-alpha)}(sigma) (with exact root alpha_min = (8-sqrt(46))/18) are algebraically clean and numerically verified by hand.
weaknesses: Core equivalence (i)<=>(iv) is already subsumed by pure-reference quantum dichotomy theory [5-7], and Theorems 4-5 are largely elementary calculus, determinant, and rank-counting applications of Theorem 2.
Unresolved mathematical errors and overclaims in Theorem 4(a) (C^1 tangency at Delta_q=0), Theorem 5(b) (minimal Kraus rank for r_Delta >= 2), and Theorem 2's perturbation phrasing.
Conceptual overstatement in Theorem 5(a)/Section 4 framing a 1D integral-order separation (already present for D=2 qubits) as a D >= 3 quantum-coherence advantage beyond Blackwell majorization.

Severe reproducibility gap in the PDF: zero concrete repository URLs and zero SHA-256 digests appear despite prominent claims of 16 SHA-256 certificates, Lean proofs, and 56 pytest checks; Lean does not verify the main analytic sufficiency theorem; and theorem numbering clashes throughout (Theorems 1-3 vs. 2, 4, 5).
potential_errors: In Theorem 4(a), the statement asserts unconditional C^1 tangency at s_0^* = r_0 + r_0^2 Delta_q / x_0^2 while explicitly including Delta_q = 0; at Delta_q = 0, s_0^* = r_0 and the boundary has a slope jump of x_0/(2r_0) (left derivative x_0/(2r_0) vs. right derivative 0), so it is only C^0. Also, C^1 tangency for Delta_q > 0 is never proved in the proof of Theorem 4.

In Theorem 5(b), the claim that 'the normal-form channel of de Leon's Theorem 2 has minimal Kraus rank 1 + r_T max(1, r_Delta)' is false for general normal-form CP remainders Phi when r_T >= 2 and r_Delta >= 2 (it holds only for the rank-1-Choi measure-and-prepare ansatz Phi(Z) = Tr[(I-T^dagger T)Z] omega). Theorem 3(a) provides a valid, explicit S_{d+1}-invariant 5-tensor family across all d >= 2 and all fields with char(F) nmid (d+1), proved rigorously via a (d+1)x(d+1) Schur complement, upgrading Vrana-Zuiddam's single d=2, t=1/2 counterexample to unbounded subadditivity violations for all strictly interior weights t in (0,1).

assessments.summary: This manuscript is a modest technical follow-up to Aiger, Har-Peled, and Zuzic (arXiv:2611.32334v2, [1]) studying quantitative stability, d-dimensional extensions, covering regimes, and structural sharpness within the AHZ proof of Hadwiger's 3D covering conjecture. Its main substantive contributions are Theorem 1(a), deriving an explicit cubic stability bound eta(K) >= d_H(S_tilde, Z)^3 / 9 via the John zonotope Z and Lipschitz integration over two disjoint antipodal spherical caps, and Theorem 3(b), proving pointwise constant generic shadow-boundary Z-length 4 sum ||z_i||_Z for all 3D zonotopes. The remaining results are direct or elementary extensions of [1]: verbatim d-dimensional versions of [1, Lemma 3.4] and [1, Theorem 5.3] (Theorem 1(b)), substituting 2m for 12 and evaluating [1, Lemma 6.4(iii)] across 11 canonical 3D bodies (Theorem 2), and brief checks on S-diameter chords and epsilon-rounded cubes (Theorem 3(a),(c)). While the core identities and Table 1 values check out mathematically, major revision is needed for compressed proof steps (omitting the polytope-to-body Fatou step in Theorems 1(a)(3) and 2(a), and an unexplained eta/24 vs eta/12 gap), overclaiming boundary-curve sharpness in Theorem 3(a), overstating Lean's formalization scope, and omitting all public URLs and SHA-256 hashes from the PDF.
strengths: Theorem 1(a) establishes a clean, explicit cubic stability bound eta(K) >= d_H(S_tilde, Z)^3 / 9 with optimal exponent 3 via comparison to the John zonotope Z and Lipschitz integration over two disjoint antipodal spherical caps.

Theorem 3(b) proves a clean, general structural theorem showing every 3D zonotope has pointwise constant generic shadow-boundary Z-length 4 sum ||z_i||_Z (zero directional variance across G(Z)), unifying the cube (12), hexagonal prism (10), and rhombic dodecahedron and truncated octahedron (8).

Theorem 2(b) and Table 1 accurately evaluate Euclidean and exact Minkowski Lemma 6.4(iii) shadow lengths across canonical 3D bodies, identifying the exact 4/pi outer-polytope zig-zagging gap on B^3, strict regime jumps on the octahedron/tetrahedron/cuboctahedron, and the dodecahedron-icosahedron ordering reversal.

Theorem 1(b)(ii) cleanly establishes the d-dimensional John mean-width ceiling d * kappa_d and parallelepiped equality characterization, and Theorem 3(c) gives an exact linear benchmark K_epsilon with sharp AHZ jump at epsilon > 1/2.
weaknesses: Strictly scoped as a modest follow-up to a single preprint [1] (arXiv:2611.32334v2): Theorem 1(b)(i)-(ii) are verbatim higher-dimensional translations (1D curve covering does not resolve d >= 4 shadow boundaries), Theorem 2(a) merely substitutes 2m for 12 (with m <= 3 vacuous everywhere and m = 4 vacuous in Euclidean), and Theorem 3(a),(c) are 4-5 line elementary checks.

Theorem 1(a)(3) provides an explicit homothety bound only for the 6 shadow-boundary translates (lambda_Sigma), leaving the 2 polar translates from {+/- w_*} unquantified and thus not yielding a full quantitative Hadwiger covering constant lambda(K) < 1.

Theorem 2(b) states John's position for symmetric bodies with irreducible point groups without verifying the John contact weights for the reducible-group bodies (hexagonal prism P_6 and cylinder C), and Theorem 2(a) leaves the one-line illumination step from a homothet cover to a direction implicit.

Minor notation errors appear: h_S instead of h_{S_tilde} in Theorem 2(a) (p. 3), and listing 6 contact points +/- e_1, +/- e_2, +/- e_3 with only 3 weights c_tilde_1 = c_tilde_2 = c_tilde_3 = 1 on p. 8.
potential_errors: Theorem 1(a)(3) and Theorem 2(a) apply [1, Theorem 6.5] directly to arbitrary non-polytopal convex bodies K to obtain L_S(gamma_{w_*}) <= 12 - eta(K) and < 2m, whereas p. 2 summarizes [1, Theorem 6.5] as giving the average bound for polytopes P and L_S < 12 for general K; extending from polytopes to general K requires lower semicontinuity of variation plus Fatou's lemma (especially given the 4/pi zig-zagging gap on B^3), which is omitted.

In Theorem 1(a)(3), the theorem statement claims lambda_Sigma <= max(1/2, 1 - eta(K)/24) and relegates 1 - eta(K)/12 to a parenthetical 'infimal ratio', yet the proof on p. 5 immediately asserts L_{S_tilde} <= 12 - eta(K) and derives 1 - eta(K)/12 without explaining why the main statement weakens it by a factor of 2.

Theorem 2(a) asserts the implication for all m in {1,...,6}, but B^3 <= S_tilde forces 8 int h_{S_tilde} >= 8 (making m=1,2,3,4 vacuous) and Golab's theorem on the projected 2D body forces L_S(Sigma(P,w)) >= 6 (making m=1,2,3 vacuous, since c(K) <= 3 is impossible in R^3).

Theorem 3(b): Universal Zero-Variance Zonotope Theorem establishing pointwise constant generic shadow-boundary length L_Z(Sigma(Z,w)) === 4 sum_{i=1}^k ||z_i||_Z across all 3D zonotopes.
Theorem 2(b): exact Minkowski-vs-Euclidean gap evaluation across canonical 3D bodies, including the 4/pi outer-polytope zig-zagging gap on B^3 and dodecahedron-icosahedron ordering reversal.

Moreover, (3) states max(1/2, 1 - eta(K)/24) in the theorem while deriving max(1/2, 1 - eta(K)/12) in the proof.

For strictly convex bodies such as B^3, every curve on dB^3 of length 2 lies in a spherical cap of radius sin(1) < 1 and IS covered by a smaller homothet, so length 2 is not sharp on dK for all K.

assessments.summary: This paper provides a brilliant, rigorous, and fully certified resolution of the four open problems and gaps posed in Rossi's recent preprint on the permutohedron face lattice. By constructing explicit all-integer primal weight tables, infinite-support LP-dual barriers, combinatorial mode enclosures, exact zero-float quotient Dinic max-flows, and closed-form equitable network flows, the author settles the exact asymptotic weight-table limits (75/104, 233/323, and 257935/357572), proves Rossi's conjectured threshold n_0 = 614 unconditionally, extends the Sperner property rigorously to n <= 25, and establishes the complete dichotomy for the normalized matching property (NMP). All mathematical developments are formally verified in Lean 4 (zero sorry) and reproduced via a zero-float Python verifier with published SHA-256 manifest hashes.
strengths: Definitive resolution of all four open problems from Rossi (2026)
Complete, self-contained proofs combining exact LP duality, recurrences, and max-flows
Formal verification in Lean 4 with zero sorry and rigorous AST-audited Python verification
Explicit public repository URL and SHA-256 certificate hash included in the PDF
weaknesses: Scoped as a specialized follow-up to a single recent preprint, limiting broader immediate cross-domain visibility outside extremal combinatorics and poset theory
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact infinite-support LP-dual barriers for local weight tables on permutohedron face lattices
Closed-form equalizing Kn-1 quotient flow proving universal positive NMP at j = n - 2

Minor issues are missing A/2 > 0, C > 0 hypotheses in Theorem 1(b) and compressed Theorem 3(a) asymptotics; cert08-cert10 (n <= 1164 mode check, n <= 25 Dinic flows) cannot be audited from the PDF alone.

rigor.basis: Proofs of Theorem 1(a) and Theorem 3(b)-(c) are clean and self-contained given Tables 1-2. Rigor is reduced by: (1) overclaiming complete settlement of Open Question 2 while leaving (1-ln 2)n/ln n <= j <= n-3 open; (2) omitting A/2 > 0, C > 0 in Theorem 1(b), allowing degenerate ratio counterexamples; (3) compressing the (1+1/j)^n vs e^{n/j} bound (ignoring e^{-O(n/j^2)} for bounded/sqrt(n) j) and omitting cert11's upper bound in Theorem 3(a); and (4) externalizing cert08-cert10.

Genuine mathematical contributions are the exact infinite-support LP-dual barriers (notably the 16-constraint dual pinning down 257935/357572 via split (1,8,1)->(1,4,4,1)), the elementary strict-slack reduction for n_0 = 614, the explicit (20,3) child-collision witness, and the closed-form K_{n-1} equalizing flow establishing NMP at j = n-2 for all n >= 3.

significance.basis: Resolves three of Rossi's four questions: exact limits of the linear local weight-table method, effective threshold n_0 = 614, and exact Sperner certification of OP_n up to n <= 25, plus sharp sublinear failure and j = n-2 NMP. However, the central Sperner problem inside the remaining window of width ~1.97e-4*n stays open (and is proved unreachable by Rossi's linear method), and NMP remains wide open for linear and bounded-codimension j.
