assessments.summary: This follow-up to Rossi (arXiv:2611.34537v1) makes solid, mathematically genuine progress on three fronts while falling short of its claimed complete resolution of Open Question 2. First, Theorem 1 supplies explicit all-integer primal tables (S=8, S=10) narrowing Rossi's unverified Sperner window by 21.65x to (75/104, 257935/357572) and proves via explicit finite-support LP duals that 75/104, 233/323, and 257935/357572 are the exact global barriers across arbitrary (even infinite) support within Rossi's linear paradigm. Second, Theorem 2 combines strict primal slack with log-concavity to enter Rossi's window for n >= 1164 and delegates n <= 1164 recurrence checks and n <= 25 (S_n x C_2)-quotient Dinic max-flows to an external verifier, settling n_0 = 614 and OP_n Sperner for n <= 25. Third, Theorem 3 proves NMP failure for sublinear j <= (1-eps)(1-ln 2)n/ln n, explains (20,3) via an explicit orbit-collision witness (928/3 < N_4/N_3), and constructs a neat closed-form K_{n-1} equalizing flow proving NMP at j = n-2 for all n >= 3. However, major revision is needed to walk back the overclaim that Open Question 2 is completely settled (linear and bounded-codimension j remain open), restore positivity hypotheses A/2, C > 0 in Theorem 1(b), and tighten the compressed Theorem 3(a) asymptotics.
strengths: Completely settles the exact limits of Rossi's linear local weight-table paradigm across arbitrary (even infinite) support via explicit integer primal tables (w_A, u_mon, u_ex) and elementary finite-support LP-dual certificates (especially the 16-constraint dual with split (1,8,1)->(1,4,4,1) pinning down 257935/357572).

Clever, elementary strict-slack reduction in Theorem 2(a) turning local flow slack on (1,...,1,n-j) and log-concavity into effective mode localization (n >= 1164 analytically, n_0 = 614 via exact recurrence), avoiding heavy renewal/saddle-point analysis.

Clean exact (20,3) child-collision calculation on S_bal = {(7,7,6),(7,6,7),(6,7,7)} rigorously explaining why NMP fails via 2-block sharing (928/3 < N_{20,4}/N_{20,3}) even though every singleton passes (314 > N_{20,4}/N_{20,3}).
Elegant, self-contained closed-form K_{n-1} incidence-graph equalizing flow in Theorem 3(c) proving NMP holds at j = n-2 for all n >= 3.
Transparent disclosure of exact URL, manifest SHA-256 hash, AI assistance, and explicit separation of Lean-checked algebraic identities from Python-computed finite checks.
weaknesses: Entirely scoped to a single recent preprint (Rossi, arXiv:2611.34537v1) and leaves the central open problem—closing the remaining Hall window of asymptotic width 1.9738e-4*n to prove OP_n is Sperner for all n—unresolved.

Key computational claims in Theorem 2 (integer recurrence checks for 1 <= n <= 1164 in cert08, and the 10 Dinic max-flows on quotient graphs up to 122,661 x 50,556 folded orbits in cert09-cert10) cannot be independently verified from the PDF alone, and individual cert SHA-256 hashes are omitted.

Section 5 mentions a 'full exact NMP sweep for 3 <= n <= 15' whose results are never stated in any theorem or table in the paper, and certificates cert07, cert13, cert15 are never cited in Sections 2-4.
Overclaiming complete settlement of Open Question 2 in the Abstract and Introduction despite Theorem 3 leaving the vast majority of (n, j) pairs (linear and fixed-codimension j <= n-3) open.
potential_errors: In Theorem 1(b), the ratio bounds 2B/(A/2) <= 75/104 and 2B/C >= 233/323, 257935/357572 require A/2 > 0 and C > 0; as written, degenerate triples satisfying all stated inequalities such as (w, A/2, B) = (0, -2, -1) and (u, C, B) = (0, -1, 0) violate the claimed ratio bounds.

In Section 4.1 (Theorem 3(a)), comparing e^{n/j} against 2j*2^{n/j} ignores the (1 - O(1/j))^{n/j} loss in ((1+1/j)^j)^{n/j}; a valid uniform proof for 2 <= j <= (1-eps)(1-ln 2)n/ln n must split bounded j (via (9/4)^q) from large j (via ln((1+1/j)^j) - ln 2 >= (1-eps/2)(1-ln 2)).

In Section 4.1, exact singleton failure thresholds n_sing(2..10) are stated via cert11 without specifying the upper n range checked (up to the Bonferroni threshold (9/8)^q > 2j) to rule out non-monotonicity between n_sing(j) and the Bonferroni regime.

In Section 4.1, the text divides (j+1)^n - (j+1)j^n <= N_{n,j+1} by N_{n,j} <= j^n without noting that the resulting inequality N_{n,j+1}/N_{n,j} >= (1+1/j)^n - (j+1) requires N_{n,j+1} >= 0 when the RHS is negative (though the inequality itself remains true).

Theorem 1(a) states strictness N_{n,j} < N_{n,j+1} for n >= 4 (true, though already valid for n = 3 at j = 1) and states in Section 4.1 that (6,1,6,7) and (7,6,1,6) are two compositions in L_4 rather than two S_{20}-orbits of compositions (immediately clarified by 7w_0 in the next sentence).
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact infinite-support LP-dual barriers (75/104, 233/323, and 257935/357572 via the single split (1,8,1)->(1,4,4,1)) proving global optimality limits of Rossi's linear local weight-table paradigm for arbitrary support.
Closed-form equalizing normalized flow on the K_{n-1} edge-vertex incidence quotient proving NMP at j = n - 2 for all n >= 3.
Strict-slack combinatorial mode enclosure establishing n_0 = 614 without renewal theory or asymptotics.
Explicit child-collision mechanism on the balanced orbit {(7,7,6),(7,6,7),(6,7,7)} explaining why NMP fails at (20,3) while singletons pass.
unresolved_material_objections: Material overclaim on Open Question 2: The Abstract ('resolve these questions completely') and Section 1 ('We settle all four items... Rossi asked for which pairs (n, j) NMP holds') claim a complete characterization of NMP for (n, j). In fact, Theorem 3 only establishes failure for 2 <= j <= (1-eps)(1-ln 2)n/ln n (plus (20,3) and n_sing(2..10)) and validity for j in {1, n-2, n-1}, leaving the entire linear and bounded-codimension regime (1-ln 2)n/ln n << j <= n-3 (e.g., j = alpha*n and j = n-3) as well as intermediate n < n_sing(j) for j >= 4 completely unresolved.

Missing positivity hypotheses in Theorem 1(b): Theorem 1(b) states that 'every' pair-inequality triple satisfies 2B/(A/2) <= 75/104 and 2B/C >= 233/323, 257935/357572 without assuming A/2 > 0 or C > 0. While the linear inequalities 208B <= 75(A/2), 233C <= 646B, and 515870C <= 1430288B hold unconditionally, dividing by A/2 or C fails for degenerate triples satisfying all stated pair and split inequalities, such as (w, A/2, B) = (0, -2, -1) (giving 2B/(A/2) = 1 > 75/104) or (u, C, B) = (0, -1, 0) (giving 2B/C = 0 < 233/323).

Compressed/incomplete asymptotic step in Theorem 3(a): On page 9, arguing 'since (1+1/j)^j = e(1-O(1/j)), comparing e^{n/j} against 2j*2^{n/j} shows (e/2)^{n/j} > 2j' omits the (1-O(1/j))^{n/j} decay factor (which is exponentially small in n for fixed j and Theta(1) at j ~ sqrt(n)), and the verification cutoff for cert11 showing failure persists for all n >= n_sing(j) up to the Bonferroni regime is unstated.

assessments.summary: This paper presents exact non-asymptotic quantum query lower bounds for k-Sum and Element Distinctness using exact tensor-projector adversary duals and Stirling spectral multiplicities. By refining the negative-weight adversary method of Belovs-Špalek and Ambainis-Kokainis, the author establishes explicit zero-O bounds that eliminate asymptotic ambiguity, cancel group size q exactly, and pinpoint exact finite crossover dimensions n* where negative-weight bounds overtake the positive-weight certificate barrier. The work is backed by comprehensive mathematical proofs, 16 zero-float rational LDL^T certificates, and 20 machine-checked theorems in Lean 4.36.0.
strengths: Complete, self-contained mathematical proofs for all three main theorems.
Exact Stirling spectral multiplicity formula and eigenvalue characterization for tensor projectors.
Explicit non-asymptotic bounds with exact q-cancellation and certified leading constants ck.
Full formal verification in Lean 4.36.0 (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice) and 16 zero-float rational certificates.
weaknesses: Analysis is specialized to finite abelian groups and specific polynomial-truncated adversary structures, though fully optimal for the considered regime.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact tensor-projector minimax law and Stirling spectral multiplicities for k-Sum and Element Distinctness.
Explicit non-asymptotic q-cancelled adversary bounds and exact finite-n crossover identification.

correctness_confidence.basis: All main inequalities (2)-(11), Stirling counts, and Table 1 / crossover values verify cleanly from first principles. Minor boundary-phrasing slips appear in Theorem 2(c) (d > n-k for small n) and Theorem 3(c) (C_1 = k vs C_1 <= k when q is tiny).

rigor.basis: Sections 2-4 give complete, self-contained prose proofs of all three theorems without relying on unproved external claims, and Section 5 honestly discloses what Lean covers. Minor notational overloading of Pi_{X_0} and E_S and missing 'large n' in Thm 2(c) are easily fixed.

reproducibility.basis: A public GitHub URL with tag v1.0.0 is in the footnote, and every numerical bound in Table 1 and Theorem 3(c) can be independently checked from (10). However, zero SHA-256 digests, commit hashes, or Lean/certificate excerpts actually appear in the PDF.

assessments.summary: This 10-page paper establishes explicit, O(.)-free non-asymptotic quantum query lower bounds for k-Sum and Element Distinctness over finite abelian groups of order q >= (4k+1) C(n,k), alongside the positive-weight certificate barrier and concrete crossover dimensions n* beyond sqrt(kn). Every proof in Sections 2-4 is mathematically sound and self-contained, and all numerical bounds and crossovers (n* = 1,290 for k=2 at rho=1/79; 668 for k=3 at rho=1/119; 571 for k=4 at rho=1/159) check out directly from the closed-form rational bound (10). Mathematically, the most original result is Theorem 1(b), which gives the exact Fourier shift-class spectral decomposition of H_S P_{E_S} H_S^T with eigenvalues m/q and Stirling multiplicities S_2(k,m) prod_{j=1}^{m-1}(q-j) identically for both k-Sum and Element Distinctness (k=2). However, the core block-adversary lower-bound architecture in Theorem 2 is fundamentally a non-asymptotic, explicit-constant refinement of Belovs-Spalek (2013) [6], and Theorem 3(a)-(b) reprove the classical positive-weight certificate barrier [2, 9] and k-Threshold tightness. While the footnote supplies a public GitHub URL (v1.0.0) and Section 5 transparently delineates Lean's algebraic scope from prose spectral proofs, no concrete SHA-256 hashes appear in the PDF despite citing 16 certificates. Minor precision and reproducibility revisions are warranted.
strengths: Theorem 1(b) gives an exact, self-contained Fourier shift-class spectral decomposition of H_S P_{E_S} H_S^T for every finite abelian group of order q >= 2 and every k >= 1, proving eigenvalues m/q with Stirling multiplicities S_2(k,m) * prod_{j=1}^{m-1}(q-j) and exact equivalence with Element Distinctness at k=2.

Theorem 1(a) and 1(c) cleanly prove the minimax optimality and uniqueness of the linear ramp (alpha_j = 1 - j/k) for single-subset Hadamard query differences and the scaled-isometry / trace identities on E_S.

Theorem 2 delivers a completely explicit, O(.)-free closed-form rational lower bound (10) in which q cancels cleanly between numerator and denominator, yielding verified asymptotic constants (c_2 > 0.428, c_3 > 0.341, c_4 > 0.299) and exact finite-n crossovers verified by hand from (10).
All proofs in Sections 2-4 are self-contained and mathematically sound, and Section 5 honestly discloses the boundary between Lean-verified algebraic lemmas and prose analytic/spectral proofs.
weaknesses: Modest conceptual novelty: Theorem 2 follows the standard Belovs-Spalek (2013) [6] negative-weight adversary construction and bounding strategy with explicit constant tracking, without improving the asymptotic exponent or group-size condition q >= Omega(n^k).

Theorem 3(a) and 3(b) present the classical positive-weight certificate barrier [2, 9] and textbook k-Threshold tightness as one of the paper's three main structural theorems rather than clearly labeling them as expository/baseline lemmas.

Reproducibility gap in the PDF: despite repeatedly citing Certificate cert02, cert04-cert07, cert09-cert15 and claiming 16 SHA-256 certificates in certificates/MANIFEST.json, zero SHA-256 digests or commit hashes appear anywhere in the PDF.

Heavy rhetorical emphasis in the abstract and Section 5 on Lean 4.36.0 and zero-float certificates, whereas Lean only checks elementary algebraic identities, k=2,3,4 Stirling moments, and three fixed-n arithmetic inequalities rather than the core spectral or general-n bounds.
potential_errors: Theorem 2(c) specifies d in {1,...,n-k} for all n >= k+1 and then sets d = ceil((2/(k-1))^{1/(k+1)} n^{k/(k+1)}) without noting that this d exceeds n-k for the smallest valid n (e.g., for k=2 and n=3..6, such as d=3 > 1=n-k at n=3); the (c_k - o(1))n^{k/(k+1)} corollary remains asymptotically true for large n.

Theorem 3(c) writes C_1(k-SUM_{n,G}) = k and C_1(ED_{n,G}) = 2 for total functions on G^n, whereas for small q (e.g. q=2, n=3, k=2, or n > q for ED) the function is constant 1 with C_1 = 0; only C_1 <= k (resp. <= 2) holds unconditionally, though equality holds in Theorem 2's regime q >= (4k+1)*binom(n,k).

Minor notational overloading in Section 3: Pi_{X_0} acts as a row-restriction co-isometry while Pi_{X_1^{uniq}} is a column-inclusion isometry, and E_S denotes both the k-tuple hyperplane in G^k and its lifted n-tuple cylinder in G^n (p. 6).

Abstract and Introduction advertise exact crossover dimensions n* = 1,290, 668, 571 without noting that these thresholds are specific to the chosen ratio rho = 1/(40k-1) and 4-digit rational bounds on sqrt(k*rho), as properly stated in Theorem 3(c) and Table 1.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorem 1(b): Exact Stirling spectral multiplicity law mult(m/q) = S_2(k,m) * prod_{j=1}^{m-1}(q-j) for H_S P_{E_S} H_S^T across arbitrary finite abelian groups and its spectral isomorphism between 2-Sum and Element Distinctness.
Theorem 1(a) and 1(c): Exact minimax uniqueness of the linear ramp H_S(lin) under coordinate-difference Hadamard operator norm and exact scaled-isometry identity on the solution hyperplane E_S.

Theorem 2(c) and Theorem 3(c): Closed-form q-cancelled non-asymptotic adversary bound (10) with explicit leading constants c_k and explicit finite crossover dimensions n* surpassing the positive-weight barrier sqrt(kn).

assessments.summary: This paper (P6) concludes a six-paper audit of the 71 THz mitochondrial polariton hypothesis, applying rigorous bosonic thermal-loss channel capacity theorems, receiver tiers, and PLOB bounds. While mathematically rigorous and formally checked in Lean 4, the work represents an application-specific audit of an existing quantum information framework rather than a foundational mathematical breakthrough. Furthermore, reproducibility is hindered by the omission of concrete public repository URLs in the text. A minor revision is recommended to include repository links and access instructions.

assessments.summary: This 7-page manuscript (Paper P6 of a self-published audit series) applies established bosonic thermal-loss channel capacity results and the author's prior framework [4] to evaluate classical and quantum signaling limits at 71 THz, 310 K in the context of the unrefereed bioRxiv preprint [13]. Stripping away the formal-verification packaging, the paper proves no genuinely new non-trivial mathematical theorems: core results (Giovannetti-Holevo capacity, antidegradability at eta <= 1/2, PLOB bound, homodyne/heterodyne formulas, Landauer bound) are imported from [5-11], while the new analytic steps are elementary calculus/algebra corollaries. Audit from first principles reveals material defects in the PDF: (1) Theorem 1.3 and the Abstract state Q(E_{eta,N_B}) <= min(log2(eta/(1-eta)), C_Hol(eta,N_S,N_B)) for unconstrained Q, which is false in C02 (unconstrained Q ~ 1.585 b > C_Hol = 0.392 b); (2) Theorem 2.3 (Eq. 5) writes equality instead of <= and fails for 1 < M < 2 in the Holevo branch; (3) Table 1 C05 rounds lower bounds upward (>= 303.4 and >= 3,261 vs exact 303.381 and 3,260.988 zJ) and C07 omits N_S; (4) Theorem 1.2's N_dark >= 1 intensity-absorber claim fails for Poissonian dark counts and Theorem 2.2 conflates signal power with receiver reset power; and (5) zero repository URLs or SHA-256 digests appear in the PDF.
strengths: Concavity-tangent inequality in Theorem 1.1 (ln(1 + [(1-eta)N_B]^{-1}) < beta*h*nu - ln(1-eta)) is algebraically clean and yields a uniform > 2.790/eta zJ Holevo floor for eta <= 1/2.

Clean separation of three physical receiver tiers (coherent Holevo, homodyne, heterodyne) and explicit verification of the B <= nu = 71 THz finite-bandwidth lossless Holevo floor (> 1.77 zJ/bit at 0.1 pW).
Most numerical table entries (C01-C04, C06, C08-C16) and thermodynamic parameter evaluations (beta*h*nu = 10.9918, N_B = 1.684e-5) are accurately computed from CODATA 2018 constants.
weaknesses: Reactive companion audit note (P6) applying imported capacity theorems ([5-11]) and the author's prior framework ([4]) to an unrefereed preprint ([13]) with no genuinely new mathematical theorems or methods.
Heavy emphasis on external Lean 4.36.0 / Python / SHA-256 verification artifacts that cannot be located or verified from the PDF because zero repository URLs and zero SHA-256 hashes are printed.
Several formal theorem statements and table entries suffer from missing qualifiers, improper bound rounding, and unproved/overbroad physical generalizations.
Figure 1(b) plots k_B*T*ln(2)/eta as the Landauer-Holevo floor down to 0 dB (eta = 1), visually obscuring that the channel-only Holevo floor lies strictly below k_B*T*ln(2)/eta for all 0 < eta < 1.
potential_errors: Theorem 1.3 and Abstract assert Q(E_{eta,N_B}) <= min(log2[eta/(1-eta)], C_Hol(eta, N_S, N_B)) without the input photon-number constraint N_S on Q, which is mathematically false for unconstrained Q (at C02 eta=3/4, N_S=0.1, unconstrained Q ~ 1.585 b > C_Hol = 0.392 b).

Theorem 2.3 (Eq. 5) states an equality L_max = L_att * ln(P_sig / (R_min * E_bit^(0))) rather than an upper bound <=, and its Holevo branch (L >= L_att * ln 2) is invalid for 1 < M < 2 (e.g. M = 1.5 allows distances beyond L_att * ln M).

Table 1 C05 asserts E_Hol >= 303.4 zJ and E_het >= 3,261 zJ, whereas exact values are 303.381 zJ and 3,260.988 zJ; C07 omits N_S = 10^-2; C10 uses 2.7907 rather than printed 2.790 to satisfy <= 31.46 um.

Theorem 1.2 extends the heterodyne floor to any intensity absorber with N_dark >= 1 photon/mode without proof, which is false for unbounded-peak Poissonian dark-count photon counting (where capacity per photon diverges as ln(ln M) under sparse PPM).

Theorem 2.2 asserts that at eta = 1 a thermal receiver at 310 K requires P_sig > R_min * k_B * T * ln 2, conflating optical signal power P_sig with receiver bit-erasure dissipation that can be supplied locally (e.g., by ATP at the receiver).
unresolved_material_objections: Theorem 1.3 and the Abstract state Q(E_{eta,N_B}) <= min(log2[eta/(1-eta)], C_Hol(eta, N_S, N_B)) for unconstrained unassisted quantum capacity Q, which is mathematically false whenever C_Hol(eta, N_S, N_B) < Q(E_{eta,N_B})—including the paper's own benchmark C02 (eta=3/4, N_S=0.1, where C_Hol = 0.392 b < Q ~ 1.585 b). The left-hand side must be restricted to the N_S-constrained quantum capacity Q(E_{eta,N_B}, N_S).

Theorem 2.3 (Eq. 5) states L_max = L_att * ln(P_sig / (R_min * E_bit^(0))) as an equality instead of an upper bound <= (since E_bit^(0) strictly underestimates true deep-loss Holevo and finite-N_S heterodyne costs), and in the Holevo branch with E_bit^(0) = 2.790 zJ (valid only for eta <= 1/2) the stated hypothesis M > 1 contradicts L >= L_att * ln 2 and fails as a bound whenever 1 < M < 2.

Table 1 certificate C05 states E_Hol >= 303.4 zJ and E_het >= 3,261 zJ, which are strictly false because exact evaluation at eta=10^-2, N_S=10^-3 yields 303.381 zJ and 3,260.988 zJ (lower bounds rounded upward). Certificate C07 also omits its required N_S = 10^-2 parameter.

Theorem 1.2's unproved extension of E_bit^het >= h*nu*ln(2)/eta to 'any intensity absorber with N_dark >= 1 photon/mode' holds only under Gaussian/thermal noise or peak constraints, failing for unbounded-peak Poissonian dark counts; Theorem 2.2's Landauer claim similarly conflates channel signal power P_sig with receiver bit-erasure dissipation.

Material reproducibility deficit: the PDF cites MITO-POLARITON-CHANNEL-CAPACITY-CERT-1.0, Lean 4.36.0 files, a Python verifier, and certificates/MANIFEST.json with SHA-256 certificates, yet omits all public repository URLs and all actual SHA-256 hashes from the manuscript, preventing independent retrieval or verification.

assessments.summary: This paper provides a rigorous, exhaustive mathematical follow-up and sharpening of Faisal's recent breakthrough on NPT bound entanglement in Werner states. The author proves three major theorems: (1) refining the two-qubit separable fidelity ceiling to exact 1/2 via Horodecki-PPT bootstrapping and establishing continuous NPT Werner intervals; (2) collapsing the high-dimensional feasibility problem via walled Brauer Schur-Weyl duality and Artin-Wedderburn decomposition into 3x3 blocks, proving d_min = 8 as the exact sharp dimensional threshold via 23 exact rational McCormick SDP-dual certificates; and (3) constructing a sharpened d=8 witness and a universal closed-form algebraic family for all d >= 9 with Theta(1/sqrt(d)) NPT expansion rates. Backed by rigorous proofs, exact rational arithmetic certificates, and Lean 4 formalization, the work resolves open structural questions with exemplary technical depth, calibrated appropriately as a premier follow-up contribution.
strengths: Brilliant application of walled Brauer Schur-Weyl duality and Artin-Wedderburn theory to collapse high-dimensional matrix feasibility into low-dimensional pure-integer blocks. Exquisite execution of exact rational McCormick SDP-dual certificates and rigorous zero-float verification. Complete mathematical proofs and comprehensive structural refinements.
weaknesses: As a direct reactive follow-up to a preprint published only days prior, its foundational premise builds directly upon Faisal's core state construction and coherence inequality framework.
potential_errors: None identified within the stated assumptions; all algebraic identities, Gram matrix positivity conditions, and McCormick relaxations are verified by exact rational arithmetic.
strong_novelty_candidates: Artin-Wedderburn collapse of walled Brauer algebras B_{3,1}(d) via pure-integer Gram-twisted representations and exact rational McCormick SDP dual certificates for dimensional thresholds.

correctness_confidence.basis: Independent symbolic and SDP checks confirm Theorem 1, Eqs. (12)-(17), all 24 shifted positive-coefficient Sylvester minors of Q(d), and Table 2's numerical bounds. However, Theorem 2(a) asserts a false 'if and only if' for individual Q, Section 4 silently drops 7 imaginary Hermitian parameters without invoking Q -> (Q+conj(Q))/2, page 8 omits a 1/2 factor in e_a^(eps), and Theorem 2(c)'s 23 duals cannot be audited from the PDF alone.

rigor.basis: Theorem 1 and Theorem 3(b)-(c) are mathematically solid once scaled properly. By contrast, Theorem 2 suffers from a literally false equivalence in part (a), an unstated real-symmetrization reduction from 24 to 17 real coordinates in Section 4.1-4.2, externalized intervals/duals and unspecified M_lambda(B_pi) tables in part (c), and an unproved optimality claim ('optimal asymptotic width') in Question 3. Lean covers only elementary algebraic lemmas.

novelty.basis: Immediate follow-up to Faisal [1] importing its core entanglement-distillation mechanism (Lemmas 4-6). Theorem 1 is a routine extension (already sketched for projectors in [1]). Real originality lies in the pure-integer Gram-twisted walled Brauer SDP reduction, establishing the sharp threshold d_min=8 for covariant certificates, and especially the closed-form universal family Q(d) proving Theta(1/sqrt(d)) NPT bound entanglement for all d>=9.

Within Faisal's mechanism, proving exact separability of 2-qubit outputs, resolving d_min=8, and establishing continuous Theta(1/sqrt(d)) bands across all d>=9 are clear quantitative advances.

(12), (14), and (15) explicitly print Q_8^* and Q(d), enabling direct independent verification of Theorem 3(b)-(c). assessments.summary: This reactive follow-up to Faisal (arXiv:2611.34921v1) imports Faisal's core distillation bound (Lemmas 4-6) as a black box and advances it in three directions. Theorem 1 lowers the separable-operation Bell-fidelity ceiling from (1+sqrt(2))/4 to 1/2 via HHH97 on Kraus outputs and lifts single certified Werner points to continuous intervals via local depolarization; these are valid but elementary arguments. Theorems 2 and 3 provide the substantial original mathematics: a pure-integer Gram-twisted Artin-Wedderburn collapse of the walled Brauer algebra B_{3,1}(d) showing d_min = 8 (d_crit ~ 7.2384) for covariant local-map certificates, a +34.18% sharpened d=8 integer witness Q_8^*, and an explicit closed-form algebraic family Q(d) certifying Theta(1/sqrt(d))-wide NPT bound-entangled Werner intervals for all d >= 9 simultaneously. Independent first-principles verification confirms Eqs. (12)-(17), all 24 shifted positive-coefficient Sylvester minors of Q(d), and the Table 2 bounds. However, major revision is required due to a false 'if and only if' in Theorem 2(a), an omitted 24-to-17 real-symmetrization step in Section 4, an unproved 'optimal asymptotic width' claim in Section 1, and complete omission from the PDF of Theorem 2(c)'s 23 subintervals/duals and all claimed SHA-256 hashes.
strengths: Theorem 3(c) provides an explicit, closed-form algebraic family Q(d) in Eqs. (14)-(15) whose 24 shifted Sylvester minor polynomials in t = sqrt(d)-3 all have strictly positive rational coefficients, certifying continuous Theta(1/sqrt(d))-wide bands of NPT bound-entangled Werner states across every integer dimension d >= 9 simultaneously (independently verified from first principles).

Theorem 3(b) constructs an explicit 6-entry-sparse integer witness Q_8^* in Eq. (12) expanding Faisal's certified d=8 NPT excess |8*alpha|-1 by +34.18% to alpha_8^* = -1000/7559 (all 24 Sylvester minors and Condition (2d) independently verified).

Theorem 2 identifies a clean pure-integer Gram-twisted Artin-Wedderburn block diagonalization of the 24-dimensional walled Brauer algebra B_{3,1}(d), proves B_pi^{Gamma_in} = SWAP_{01} B_{sigma pi sigma} SWAP_{01} stays inside B_{3,1}(d), and shows Condition (2d) collapses J-Q to at most 2x2 active blocks, yielding the exact dimensional threshold d_min = 8 (d_crit ~ 7.2384 independently corroborated).

Theorem 1 establishes that every two-qubit output of a separable operation on coherence-bounded states is PPT and separable (sharpening Bell fidelity to 1/2) and extends bound-entangled Werner points to continuous intervals [alpha_0, -1/d).
weaknesses: Imports Faisal's core distillation mechanism (Lemmas 4-6 of [1]) as an unverified black box and addresses only Faisal's restricted U(d)-covariant class, leaving open non-covariant certificates and the d=3,4 DiVincenzo-Dur conjectures.

Theorem 1 consists of elementary arguments (~20 lines total), with part (a) applying HHH97 to individual Kraus terms (already noted for rank-2 projectors in [1]), part (b) repeating an elementary minor bound for separability, and part (c) applying standard Werner depolarization.

Heavy framing emphasis on engineering packaging (20 Lean lemmas covering mostly elementary algebra/arithmetic, 16 external certificates, 56 tests) over self-contained presentation of the 23 SDP duals and exact representation conventions in the manuscript itself.
Minor normalization omission (missing 1/2 factor) in defining e_a^(eps) on page 8 relative to the stated Gram matrices G_+(d) and G_-(d).
potential_errors: Theorem 2(a) (p. 4) falsely states a fixed Hermitian Q satisfies (2) 'if and only if' its U(d)-Haar twirl Q-bar lies in B_{3,1}(d) and satisfies (2); adding any orthogonal perturbation R (Haar twirl 0) violating PSDness or (2d) gives a counterexample to the 'if' direction.

Section 4.1-4.2 (pp. 8-9) reduces an arbitrary complex Hermitian Q in B_{3,1}(d) (24 real parameters: 10 self-adjoint + 7 complex pairs) to 17 real coordinates q_1..q_{17} and real symmetric M_lambda(Q) without proving/invoking entrywise complex conjugation Q -> (Q + conj(Q))/2.
Page 8 defines e_a^(eps) = D_{(a,x,y)} + eps D_{(a,y,x)} without a 1/2 projector factor, which gives Gram matrix 4*G_eps(d) rather than G_eps(d) = (d - eps) I_3 + eps J_3.

Page 2 Question 3 claims an explicit family 'with optimal asymptotic width' and claims to answer all three questions 'completely', without proving a converse lower bound w_d = Omega(sqrt(d)) (i.e., |alpha(d)| = O(1/sqrt(d))) for large d.
Theorem 2(c) relies entirely on external JSON dual vectors and unprinted subinterval partitions [L, U] for d=3..7, and zero SHA-256 hashes appear in the PDF.
strong_novelty_candidates: Closed-form universal algebraic family Q(d) (Eqs. 14-15) certifying continuous Theta(1/sqrt(d)) NPT bound-entangled Werner intervals for all dimensions d >= 9 simultaneously via shifted positive-coefficient Sylvester minors.

Pure-integer Gram-twisted Artin-Wedderburn collapse of B_{3,1}(d) with Condition (2d) 2x2 block reduction establishing d_min = 8 as the sharp dimensional threshold of Faisal's covariant local-map framework.
Sharpened d=8 integer certificate Q_8^* achieving a +34.18% expansion in NPT excess.
unresolved_material_objections: False logical equivalence in Theorem 2(a) (p. 4): a fixed Hermitian matrix Q satisfies (2) 'only if' (not 'if and only if') its U(d)-Haar twirl Q-bar lies in B_{3,1}(d) and satisfies (2); Theorem 2(a) must be corrected to an existence equivalence or one-way implication.

Unproved 24-to-17 real parameter reduction in Theorem 2(c) / Sections 4.1-4.2 (pp. 8-9): complex Hermitian matrices in B_{3,1}(d) span 24 real dimensions (10 self-adjoint plus 7 complex conjugate pairs), and the proof omits the entrywise complex-conjugation symmetrization Q -> (Q + conj(Q))/2 required to restrict to 17 real coordinates and real symmetric M_lambda(Q).

Non-self-contained proof of Theorem 2(c) and missing cryptographic hashes: neither the 23 subinterval partitions [L, U] nor the 23 rational dual vectors in Q^{53}/Q^{56} (nor explicit M_lambda(B_pi) tables/indexing conventions) appear in the PDF, and zero SHA-256 hashes appear anywhere in the PDF despite repeated claims of '16 SHA-256 certificates'.

Material overclaim of 'optimal asymptotic width' in Question 3 (p. 2): the paper claims to construct a d >= 9 family 'with optimal asymptotic width' and answer Question 3 'completely', yet proves no converse lower bound w_d = Omega(sqrt(d)) (|alpha(d)| = O(1/sqrt(d))) ruling out wider covariant certificates as d -> infinity.

assessments.summary: This paper performs a rigorous quantitative stability, perturbation-order separation, and independent zero-float Bernstein certification study across the Hales-Xue framework for the Reinhardt conjecture. Theorem 1 establishes the exact second-order stability curvature and global elementary quantitative stability bounds for four-arc all-forward disks. Theorem 2 proves the global strict convexity and linear defect of Hales' six-arc mixed family, establishing a precise linear-vs-quadratic stability dichotomy with regular-walk spectra. Theorem 3 independently reconstructs and certifies all 576 tensor Bernstein coefficients of Claim V11 and 2,700 coefficients of Claim V6 in pure rational arithmetic, auditing parameter sharpness. While building as a reactive follow-up to November 2026 preprints, the mathematical depth, exact algebraic proofs, and Lean 4 formalization are executed with exemplary rigor.
strengths: Rigorous closed-form computation of the exact second-order stability curvature for the four-arc closure circle.
Clean establishment of the linear-vs-quadratic perturbation dichotomy between mixed and forward families.
Flawless independent pure-rational tensor Bernstein certification for Claims V11 and V6 without floating-point arithmetic.
weaknesses: As a reactive follow-up to very recent preprints, its conceptual novelty is bounded by existing frameworks.
Lack of explicit URLs or raw hash strings in the static PDF text.
potential_errors: Omission of explicit repository URLs and concrete SHA-256 hash strings directly in the PDF text limits immediate offline reproducibility without supplementary files.

correctness_confidence.basis: The 1D calculus identities and numerical bounds in Theorems 1 and 2(a) and Table 1 (m=1..8) verify cleanly from first principles. However, Theorem 2(b) omits any proof for the infinite tail m>=9 while asserting global monotonicity and uniqueness, Theorem 3 omits all polynomial and box-guard definitions (preventing independent verification), and Section 5 contains an invalid pointwise-to-polynomial divisibility deduction and an incomplete slope-sign quantifier.

rigor.basis: Rigorous only in the elementary 1D calculus derivations of Theorems 1 and 2(a). Theorem 2(b) commits a major finite-to-infinite gap by claiming global strict monotonicity, limits, and uniqueness across all N=3m+1 (m>=1) solely from interval checks at m=1..8. Section 5 lacks definitions of the Claim V11/V6 polynomials and six box guards, infers polynomial divisibility in Q[p1..p5] from a pointwise implication P=0 => L^2-B=0, and checks a_{1,i}<0 only on active constraints for unboundedness.

novelty.basis: Modest companion note to Hales (2026) and Xue (2026) that imports all reductions, explicit formulas (Anorm, Amix, delta_N, det S_N), and Bernstein certificate formulations (Claims V6, V11). Theorems 1 and 2(a) are elementary single-variable calculus exercises on two fixed 1D families from Hales; Theorem 2(b) evaluates 8 finite points; Theorem 3 re-verifies Hales' certificates via exact rational collocation and 1D linear feasibility. No genuinely new deep theorems are proved.

significance.basis: Provides concrete 1D curvature and stability constants (c_s, c_theta, lambda_mix) along two specialized trajectories in Hales' proof and audits rational parameter margins for Claim V11 along 1D slices. Does not establish quantitative stability for general centrally symmetric convex disks or general optimal-control walks, and leaves the overarching Hales-Xue proof structure unchanged.

reproducibility.basis: Despite claiming 16 SHA-256 JSON certificates, 20 Lean 4.36.0 theorems, and 56 pytest checks, the PDF contains zero public repository URLs, zero commit or archive identifiers, and zero actual SHA-256 hashes—only local relative file paths and opaque labels (cert01-cert16). Moreover, the Claim V11/V6 polynomials, six box guards, and certified ln 2 rational brackets are omitted from the PDF, preventing independent verification.

assessments.summary: Isolated PDF-only reassessment of a reactive companion note to Hales (2026) and Xue (2026) on the Reinhardt conjecture. The paper computes exact 1D stability bounds along two specialized trajectories imported from Hales—the four-arc closure circle (Theorem 1: exact curvature at pi/4 and global elementary s- and quadratic bounds) and the six-arc mixed family (Theorem 2(a): strict convexity and linear lower bound)—evaluates 8 points of the regular-walk branch N=3m+1 (Theorem 2(b)), and reports an exact rational Bernstein collocation re-verification and 1D affine sensitivity check for Hales' Claims V11 and V6 (Theorem 3). While the explicit calculus calculations in Theorems 1 and 2(a) and Table 1 (m=1..8) are arithmetically accurate, the mathematical depth is elementary and scoped strictly to imported 1D curves rather than general convex disks. Crucially, several material issues block acceptance: Theorem 2(b) asserts infinite strict monotonicity, limits, and uniqueness across all m>=1 from evaluations at m=1..8 with zero proof for m>=9; Theorem 3 omits all polynomial, box-guard, and ln 2 bracket definitions, uses a flawed pointwise-to-polynomial divisibility argument for Claim V6, and misstates the unboundedness check as requiring a_{1,i}<0 only on active constraints; scope claims ('perturbation dichotomy', 'near-optimal') overreach the 1D analyses; and the PDF contains zero repository URLs and zero SHA-256 hashes.
strengths: Theorem 1(a) correctly derives the exact closed-form second derivative A_norm''(pi/4) = (340 - 132*sqrt(2) - (80 + 90*sqrt(2))*ln 2)/49 and verifies Eq. (9) consistently from Eq. (2).

Theorem 1(b) gives a complete, valid elementary proof of the global 1D lower bound A_norm(cos theta, sin theta) - delta_oct >= c_s*(sqrt(2) - cos theta - sin theta) >= c_theta*(theta - pi/4)^2 across (0, pi/2) and the resulting Xue competitor radius |theta - pi/4| < 4.9962e-3 rad.

Theorem 2(a) accurately computes A_mix''(v) = 8*sqrt(3)/(v*(v+4)^2) > 0 and delta_mix'(v_max) = -lambda_mix < 0 for Hales' six-arc mixed formula, establishing the 1D linear defect bound delta_mix(v) - delta_oct >= lambda_mix*(v_max - v).

All reported numerical values in Table 1 (m=1..8) and derived rational comparisons in Theorems 1, 2(a), and 3 (c_s, c_theta, lambda_mix, kappa_0 - kappa_min, r_0 - r_min, 1/(4*kappa^2)) are internally arithmetically accurate.
weaknesses: Entire problem setup, geometric reductions, and core formulas (Eq. (2), Eq. (9), w_c'(x) >= (c-2)/(2x), A_mix(v), delta_N, det S_N, Claims V6 and V11) are imported directly from Hales [4] and Xue [7], leaving very limited mathematical depth (elementary 1D calculus + rational linear/Bernstein evaluation).

No quantitative stability bound is proved for general centrally symmetric planar convex disks K (nor for general N-arc optimal-control trajectories), restricting stability results strictly to two 1D parameterizations.

Severe lack of self-containedness and reproducibility in the PDF: polynomial definitions, auxiliary box guards, ln 2 rational brackets, public repository URLs, and SHA-256 hashes are completely absent.
Multiple proof gaps and overstatements in Theorems 2(b) and 3 (unproved tail m >= 9, invalid real-to-polynomial divisibility claim, active-only slope check, and 1D-slice optimality claims).
potential_errors: In Theorem 1(b) (p. 5), the proof states ln(q0_bar/q1_bar) > 2*(q0_bar - q1_bar)/s on (0, pi/4], whereas strict inequality fails at the endpoint theta = pi/4 (equality 0 = 0); harmless for the subsequent >= bound.

In Theorem 1(b) (p. 5), the derivation of max(|q0_bar - 2^{-1/2}|, |q1_bar - 2^{-1/2}|) < 3.5454e-3 in Eq. (5) from |theta - pi/4| < 4.9962e-3 omits the intermediate trigonometric bound step (though numerically true: max deviation is ~3.54165e-3).

In Proof of Theorem 1(a) (p. 4), differentiating Eq. (9) at theta = pi/4 substitutes c = 3 directly into w_c'(1/sqrt(2)) without noting that dc/dtheta|_{pi/4} = 0 and partial_c(w_c(q0_bar)-w_c(q1_bar))|_{pi/4} = 0 (both vanish, so the identity holds, though the step is compressed).
In Theorem 1(b) (p. 5), the proof cites Hales [4, Lemma 10.2] for w_c'(x) >= (c-2)/(2x) rather than proving it in-text (though it follows in two lines from 2x ln x + 1 - x^2 >= 0).

Theorem 3(b) mentions determinant cap extension from 0.183884 to 0.183950 without noting Hales' upper constraint det S < 9193/50000 = 0.18386 (which imposes kappa < ~1.166074) or upper constraints on r from the auxiliary box guards.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact closed-form curvature A_norm''(pi/4) and global elementary s-antiderivative lower bound with explicit constants c_s, c_theta along Hales' 1D four-arc closure curve.
Global strict convexity identity A_mix''(v) = 8*sqrt(3)/(v*(v+4)^2) and explicit linear defect slope lambda_mix along Hales' 1D six-arc mixed family.

1D exact rational affine-sensitivity thresholds (kappa_min, r_min) for Hales' Claim V11 tensor Bernstein certificate (conditional on publishing definitions and correcting the global slope-sign quantifier).
unresolved_material_objections: Theorem 2(b) finite-to-infinite proof gap: Evaluating delta_N and det S_N only at m in {1,...,8} (Table 1) does not prove strict monotonic convergence delta_N -> pi/(2*sqrt(3)) and det S_N -> 3/16 for all m >= 1, nor the inequality det S_N < 3/16, nor that N = 4 is the unique regular walk (over all m >= 1) below 9193/50000; no asymptotic or analytic proof is provided for the tail m >= 9 (where competing factors in det S_N make naive bounds insufficient below m = 20).

Theorem 3 is unverifiable and non-self-contained: None of the explicit algebraic formulas for Hales' Claim V11 sign/weight polynomials (P_V11, omega_1..omega_4), the six auxiliary box guards in check_winding.py, the Claim V6 five-variable polynomials (L^2, B, P, M, y, j), or the certified ln 2 rational brackets appear in the PDF.

Invalid algebraic divisibility argument in Claim V6 (Section 5, p. 7): Claiming that the pointwise implication P = 0 => M = 1, y = j = 0 => L^2 - B = 0 proves P divides L^2 - B identically in Q[p1,...,p5] is invalid without proving P is squarefree/radical over C (or verifying exact quotient multiplication in Q[p1,...,p5]); moreover, grid collocation of (L^2-B)/P on {0,1/d_r,...,1}^5 is undefined wherever P vanishes unless the quotient polynomial is computed symbolically beforehand.

Logical gap in Theorem 3(b) unboundedness proof (Section 5, p. 7): Checking a_{1,i} < 0 'on every active constraint (hence unbounded above)' does not prove the feasibility interval is (kappa_min, infinity); one must verify a_{1,i} <= 0 across all 576 Bernstein coefficients, as an inactive coefficient with a_{1,j} > 0 would impose a finite upper bound.

Material overclaims in scope and optimality: (i) Abstract and Theorem 2(a) claim an exact linear-vs.-quadratic 'perturbation dichotomy' of K_oct (and compare unnormalized coordinate radii < 2.60e-5 vs < 5.00e-3), whereas Theorems 1 and 2(a) analyze only two 1D families imported from Hales [4], not general mixed-switch vs all-forward perturbations or general convex disks, and Theorem 1 omits an explicit O((theta-pi/4)^2) upper bound; (ii) Theorem 3(b) calls (kappa_0, r_0) 'near-optimal' and 'razor-sharp' using only 1D coordinate slices, leaving the joint 2D (kappa, r) feasible region and larger-r tradeoffs unexamined.

Zero reproducibility artifacts in the PDF: No public repository URL, no code/data DOI or commit hash, and no actual SHA-256 digests appear anywhere in the manuscript, contradicting the verification/certification framing in the Abstract and Section 6.

assessments.summary: This paper presents a rigorous, mathematically complete reassessment and extension of recent work on real equiangular lines and Leech lattice sections by Djaljapayan, Liao, and Yu. The author proves four main theorems: a complete classification of positive-slope relative-bound seeds (Theorem 1), exact alternating character bounds and seed-eigenvector extensions yielding six sharp infinite families (Theorem 2), consecutive-dimension quadratic-irrational intervals and infinite block windows with an s >= 4 impossibility barrier (Theorem 3), and an unconditional resolution of the fourth generalized Hamming weight d4(C) = 204 of the Leech evaluation code along with an optimal 19-dimensional Leech section chain (Theorem 4). All results are formally verified in Lean 4.36.0 and supported by 20 cryptographic certificates.
strengths: Complete and exact classification of positive-slope relative-bound seeds (Theorem 1).
Sharp infinite families and explicit seed-eigenvector extensions (Theorem 2).
Rigorous consecutive-dimension extensions and s >= 4 block barrier (Theorem 3).
Unconditional proof of d4(C) = 204 via fourth-moment integer inequalities and explicit 19D Leech section (Theorem 4).
Exemplary formal verification in Lean 4.36.0 with 20 cryptographic certificates.

Within that scope, the circulant alternating-character bound [-3,1], explicit {±1}^M seed eigenvectors, rational k=a^2-3 branch, conference-matrix interval extension, and unconditional fourth-moment kill of Leech support 203 represent solid original technical advances.

assessments.summary: This paper systematically completes and sharpens the fixed-angle equiangular line and Leech evaluation-code program of Djaljapayan, Liao, and Yu (arXiv:2611.34855v1). Theorem 1 classifies positive-slope relative-bound seed parameters under Bukh–Cox. Theorem 2 proves an exact circulant alternating-character bound in [-3,1] and constructs {±1}^M seed eigenvectors for a=3, unlocking four new infinite families (k=3,5,6,22), sharpening k=7 (319->245) and k=23 (5599->5267), and establishing zero-gap +2 jumps. Theorem 3 extends conference-matrix points to linear intervals and s in {2,3} block windows to all odd q>=5 up to Pell barriers, proving an s>=4 relative-bound impossibility. Theorem 4 proves d_4(C)=204 unconditionally via a fourth-moment kill of the unique support-203 PG(3,2) survivor and constructs a 72-axis 19D Leech section. Auditing from first principles confirms that all formulas, Table 1 thresholds, and spectral counts are mathematically accurate. Nonetheless, the work is tightly reactive to a single preprint, delegates Theorem 4(a) Step 2, Theorem 4(b), and small-q threshold sweeps to unprinted external certificates, and leaves the third octad O_3 in Theorem 4(b) unspecified, requiring major revision to make the PDF proofs self-contained and precise.
strengths: Theorem 1 gives a clean, complete algebraic classification of positive-slope relative-bound seed parameter triples (k, M, b) for all odd a >= 3 and identifies the exact rational submaximal branch k = a^2 - 3.

Theorem 2(a)–(b) sharply improves DLY's construction via two genuine linear-algebraic ingredients: the exact alternating-character evaluation lambda_alt(A) in {-3,-2,-1,0,1} independent of r, and explicit {±1}^M seed eigenvectors for all four a=3 seeds enabling odd-t repetitions with constant Schur ratio rho_v = k/a.

All numerical thresholds in Table 1 (7, 155, 161, 245, 8643, 5267, plus Even-t and Best mod 4 columns), rational/irrational slopes, zero-gap +2 jumps (10|Q and 112|Q, plus the single-point jump at Q = 56 mod 112), and Pell boundaries (15,25) and (35,49) are mathematically verified and exact.

Theorem 3 provides completely self-contained proofs upgrading DLY Theorem 5.2 from singletons to linear intervals and DLY Proposition 5.3 to infinite s in {2,3} windows alongside an exact s >= 4 relative-bound barrier.

Theorem 4(a) Steps 1 and 3 give an ingenious, Niemeier-free fourth-moment elimination (via w' = y_{a_1} + y_{a_2} + y'_{a_3} and t^4 - 4t^2 >= -3 * 1_{t odd}) of the support-203 PG(3,2) signature, and Theorem 4(b) explicitly identifies the optimal 19D 72-axis Leech section (with rank 19 proved by the elementary trace bound 25*72/(72+24) = 18.75 > 18).
weaknesses: Tightly reactive scope built directly on DLY (arXiv:2611.34855v1), importing the core hard theorems (Bukh–Cox real coherence bound, DLY's 23-Niemeier resolution of N(18)–N(20), and DLY's Leech code moment identities and section lemma).

Heavy emphasis on formal-verification packaging ('24 Lean theorems', '20 SHA-256 certificates', '64 pytests') while Table 2 obscures that the heaviest combinatorial searches (PG(3,2) CSP in C18, Golay evaluations in C20, and finite q-sweeps in C06–C11) are performed in unprinted Python scripts rather than proved in Lean or in the PDF text.

In Theorem 1(b), the classification for odd a >= 7 applies only to abstract parameter triples (k, M, b), since existence of realized two-eigenvalue Seidel matrices for k in {a^2-3, a^2-2} when a >= 7 remains open.
Individual SHA-256 hashes for C01–C20 are absent from the PDF (only MANIFEST.json is hashed), and Theorem 2(c) omits explicit definitions for the 'Even-t' and 'Best mod 4' columns of Table 1.

Table 1 includes 'Even-t' and 'Best mod 4' threshold columns whose exact residue-class definitions are omitted from the formal statement of Theorem 2(c).
Minor editorial/artifact detail: Section 6 refers to 'verification/verify_paper106.py', an apparent leftover internal script identifier.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorem 2(a)–(b): Exact circulant alternating-character bound lambda_alt in [-3,1] (replacing Q-2r by Q-6) together with explicit {±1}^M seed eigenvectors enabling odd-t families and unlocking k in {3,5,6,22} plus zero-gap +2 jumps.

Theorem 4(a)–(b): Unconditional proof of Leech d_4(C) = 204 via 3D plane classification and the 3-way lift fourth-moment inequality t^4 - 4t^2 >= -3 * 1_{t odd}, paired with the explicit 4-normal 72-axis 19D section (y_a, y_{O_1}, y_b, y_{O_2}).

Read literally, the claim fails for arbitrary octads O_3 in G_23 (for instance, O_3 = O_1 or O_3 = O_2 yields 72 axes), and no proof is provided beyond citing external Certificate C20.

Incomplete PDF-level proofs due to reliance on unprinted external Python certificates: Theorem 4(a) Step 2 delegates the elimination of all 30,827 PG(3,2) subsets of size K >= 5 (with sum wt <= 1624) entirely to Certificate C18 without providing analytic proofs for K=5 or K in {7,8,9}; Theorem 4(b) delegates verifying the 10 Golay octads O_2, their {0, ±1} axis evaluations, and the [100^9, 112^3, 132^3] spectrum to Certificate C20 rather than giving the short S(4,7,23) design-theoretic proof; and Theorem 2(c) delegates exact small-q thresholds in Table 1 to Certificates C06–C12 without writing out the explicit residue-class inequalities mod 2b.

assessments.summary: This paper provides rigorous, closed-form analytic solutions to three prominent open problems regarding multimode Gaussian quantum networks raised by Chakrabarty (2026). Specifically, the author proves universal 3k-1 three-setting steering saturation for all k >= 1 via explicit 2n-matrix dual witnesses, establishes the exact four-setting equatorial threshold eta_eq(4) = 4/13 (surpassing the regular tetrahedron threshold), achieves a 16x asymptotic sharpening of CHSH nonlocality using an on/off photon-presence bucket detector, and derives exact Fock-Bargmann frame-permanent identities and Galois rationality for heralded multimode states. All theorems are backed by complete analytical proofs and constructive Lean 4 formal verification.
strengths: Completely resolves three open analytical problems from recent literature with closed-form, verified proofs.
Rigorously constructs explicit dual steering witnesses and evaluates permanent identities over cyclotomic number fields.
Comprehensive formal verification in Lean 4 and zero-float rational arithmetic.
weaknesses: Scope is strictly tailored as a specialized follow-up audit and extension of a single recent preprint, limiting broader conceptual independence.
strong_novelty_candidates: Closed-form analytic proof of 3k-1 steering saturation and exact n=4 equatorial thresholds for multimode Gaussian networks.

(1)-(16), dual feasibility, the SOS identity 5D(eps)>0, degree-4/6 physicality/positivity polynomials, Z[sqrt(5)] Ryser permanents (19520, 2457600), and the 1/(12k) asymptote—were verified from first principles and hold. However, Theorem 4(b) wrongly states '10.67x at k=3' for 8(2k-1)/(k+1) (actually 10x), and theorem numbering contradicts itself throughout.

(15)'s improvement on p_1 > 1/k), Theorem 4(a) omits the 4k-3k^2 derivation for theta in {0,pi/2}, Theorem 2(b) omits monotonicity for lambda*^2 <= 98/225, and the theorem counter clashes.

The equatorial+Z dual witness beating the tetrahedron at n=4 (4/13) and the all-k Galois rationality proof for frame permanents are neat original results within this specialized setting.

Useful specialized advance in CV quantum network monogamy, not a major field-level breakthrough.

assessments.summary: Follow-up to Chakrabarty (arXiv:2611.34874v1) resolving three analytic/quantitative gaps for k-mode Gaussian networks. Theorem 2 ('Thm. 1') builds a 2n-matrix rank-1 equatorial+Z dual steering witness on the 1-photon filtered subspace yielding eta_eq(n) = [1 + (n-1)^2 sin^2(pi/(2n-2))]^-1, lifts it to full Fock space, certifies SR_3^filt >= (3/80)(3*eta-1)^2 on (1/3,1] with physical squeezing lambda in (0,1) (proving 3k-1 saturation for all k >= 1), and achieves eta_eq(4)=4/13 (certifying ceil(13k/4)-1 four-setting neighbors for all k >= 1). Theorem 4 ('Thm. 2') swaps CHSH settings to neighbor bucket detection {O_pi, O_{pi/2}}, proving B(eta) >= 2 + 2(2*eta-1)^2/(1+3(2*eta-1)) (a 4x-16x prefactor gain at unchanged (2k-1)^-2 scaling). Theorem 5 ('Thm. 3') proves N_k = perm(G_k) in Q and p_1 = perm(G_k/G_00)/perm(G_k) in Q via Wick's theorem and cyclotomic Galois invariance (exact k=3 values N_3=610/243, p_1=320/549), a parity-split Wigner bound, and heralding asymptote (3/2)(4/27)^k (1 + 1/(12k) + O(k^-2)). Core identities audit cleanly, but Theorem 4(b) miscomputes k=3 as 10.67x instead of 10x, theorem numbering is internally inconsistent, p_1 > 1/k is unproved for general k >= 4, and no repo URL or SHA-256 hash appears in the PDF.
strengths: Clean, explicit, non-asymptotic dual steering witness (Lemma 1 + Theorem 2) analytically resolving all-k 3k-1 three-setting steering saturation and lowering the n=4 critical transmission to 4/13 (certifying ceil(13k/4)-1 neighbors for all k >= 1).

Exact full-Fock-space lifting of the two-qubit steering witness via F_{+/-|Z}^full = F_{+/-|Z} (+) Pi_1^perp, giving rigorous unfiltered bounds SR_n(rho_AB) >= (1 - lambda^4)(W(lambda) - 1) > 0 for physical lambda in (0,1).
Neat cyclotomic Galois automorphism invariance proof (Theorem 5(a)) establishing rationality of N_k and p_1(|Phi_k>) for all k >= 1, alongside exact Z[sqrt(5)] permanent computations at k=3.
All core rational identities, SOS polynomials, degree-4/6 positivity checks, k=2,3 permanents, and heralding asymptotics are mathematically sound upon first-principles verification.
weaknesses: Modest mathematical depth and scope: strictly a reactive follow-up to a single 2026 preprint using elementary-to-moderate tools (2x2 Schur complements, polygon geometry, low-degree polynomial positivity, photon-block expectations, basic cyclotomic Galois permutations).

Theorem 4 does not improve the asymptotic (2k-1)^-2 CHSH scaling exponent or neighbor count (only the constant prefactor), and Theorem 2(c) leaves the gap between eta_eq(4) = 4/13 (~0.3077) and the monogamy floor 1/4 open.

Theorem 5(b) yields no closed-form k-only sharpening for k >= 4 because p_1(|Phi_k>) is only evaluated explicitly up to k = 3 (relying on numerical Ryser permanents in Fig. 2(a) for k = 4, 5, 6) and p_1 > 1/k is not proved in general.

Arithmetic error at k=3 in Theorem 4(b) (10.67x vs 10x), broken internal theorem numbering throughout, and complete absence of concrete repo URLs or SHA-256 digests in the PDF despite prominent formal-verification claims.

Pervasive LaTeX theorem-numbering contradiction: Abstract, Sections 2-4 titles, Table 1, Fig. 1(a) legend, and Fig. 2(a) legend refer to Theorems 1, 2, 3, while the body environments are numbered Theorem 2, Theorem 4, Theorem 5 (sharing a counter with Lemma 1 and Remark 3), and Fig. 1 caption cites 'Theorems 2-4'.

Minor compressed/omitted steps: Theorem 5(b) does not prove p_1(|Phi_k>) > 1/k for general k >= 2 (leaving general-k improvement over -rho^2 conditional); Theorem 4(a) omits the derivation of 4*kappa - 3*kappa^2 <= 4/3 for theta in {0,pi/2}; Theorem 2(b) omits proving monotonicity of lambda*^2 on (0, 1/2] for lambda*^2 <= 98/225.
Reproducibility gap in Section 5: relative paths and 16 SHA-256 certificates are claimed, but zero repository URLs or SHA-256 hashes appear in the PDF.
strong_novelty_candidates: Equatorial+Z rank-1 dual steering witness and critical transmission eta_eq(n) = [1 + (n-1)^2 sin^2(pi/(2n-2))]^-1, analytically certifying 3k-1 three-setting steering saturation for all k >= 1 and beating the regular tetrahedron at n=4 with eta_eq(4) = 4/13 (ceil(13k/4)-1 neighbors).

Cyclotomic Galois invariance proof showing frame permanents N_k = perm(G_k) and p_1(|Phi_k>) = perm(G_k/G_00)/perm(G_k) are rational numbers in Q for every k >= 1, yielding exact k=3 values N_3 = 610/243 and p_1 = 320/549.

Swapping CHSH settings to on/off bucket detection {O_pi, O_{pi/2}} on the lossy neighbor mode to constructively align multiphoton excess (p_21 > p_20), giving a non-asymptotic 4x-16x CHSH margin sharpening.

Pervasive theorem-numbering contradiction across the manuscript: Abstract, Sections 2-4 headings, Table 1, and Figure legends cite Theorems 1, 2, 3, whereas the theorem environments are numbered Theorem 2, Theorem 4, Theorem 5 (sharing a counter with Lemma 1 and Remark 3), and Figure 1's caption refers to 'Theorems 2-4'.

Theorem 5(b) does not prove p_1(|Phi_k>) > 1/k (or give a closed-form k-only lower bound on p_1) for general k >= 4, leaving the general-k Wigner improvement over Chakrabarty's Theorem 5 conditional on p_1 > 1/k; additionally, Theorem 4(a) omits the 4*kappa - 3*kappa^2 derivation for theta in {0, pi/2} and Theorem 2(b) omits monotonicity for lambda*^2 <= 98/225.

assessments.summary: This paper presents a definitive mathematical resolution of the orthogonal minimax coherence problem µ_R(d) across non-Hadamard residue classes d \equiv 2 \pmod 4 and all odd dimensions d \geq 3. Through rigorous pure-polynomial inequalities, Hadamard sign-parity obstructions, and Seidel matrix spectral rigidity, the author establishes exact arithmetic dichotomies, unique tightness at d=3, explicit rational circulant witnesses in SO(5, Q) and SO(7, Q), and exhaustive \mathbb{Z}[\zeta_{24}] cyclotomic ring classifications for MUB-6. The mathematical analysis is complemented by a dual verification framework consisting of 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems (0 sorry) and 16 zero-float Python certificates.
strengths:
1. Definitive resolution of orthogonal minimax coherence for d \equiv 2 \pmod 4 and odd dimensions.
2. Rigorous spectral-divisibility and Seidel matrix rigidity proofs.
3. Exhaustive exact cyclotomic ring search certifying the MUB-6 obstruction.
4. Exceptional dual formal verification (Lean 4 and zero-float Python certificates).
weaknesses: The results are specialized to combinatorial matrix theory and quantum information theory, requiring advanced algebraic machinery.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact resolution of orthogonal minimax coherence across d = 2 mod 4 and odd dimensions via conference-matrix rigidity and spectral Seidel matrix divisibility.

correctness_confidence.basis: All proofs of Theorems 1(a)-(c), 2(a)-(c), and 3(a) were audited line by line from first principles and are mathematically sound, as are the explicit rational circulants U5 and U7. The 12-ray 2K_{3,3} complement spectrum in Theorem 3(b) matches the tensor-product family Y_2 tensor (M_1 U M_2) in C^2 tensor C^3, though the exhaustive 24^5 search itself cannot be re-executed from the PDF alone.

rigor.basis: The human mathematical arguments in Sections 2-3 are concise, elementary, and rigorous across all parity, partial-zero (|N0| >= 3, 1, 2), and Seidel spectral-divisibility cases, and Section 5 transparently restricts Lean's claims to the scalar/divisibility/single-witness kernel. Rigor is penalized by overstated claims in the Abstract and Intro claiming 'complete resolution' of d = 2 mod 4 and an 'exact arithmetic dichotomy'.

novelty.basis: Theorems 1 and 2 prove genuinely new, self-contained results settling the open conference-matrix rigidity conjecture for d = 2 mod 4 (e.g. mu_R(6)=1/sqrt(5)) and establishing the sharp odd-d bound 2/sqrt(4d-3) with unique d=3 tightness. However, the proofs use short elementary polynomial/parity/spectral arguments, Theorem 3(a) is an immediate corollary, and Theorem 3(b) rediscovers a known 12th-root subset of Grassl's (2004) unrestricted C^6 classification without citing Grassl or Jaming-Matolcsi (2015).

significance.basis: Resolves mu_R(d) = 1/sqrt(d-1) for all conference-matrix orders d = 2 mod 4 and gives clean real MUB excess bounds. Yet exact values remain open for all Belevitch-obstructed d = 2 mod 4 (d=22,34,...) and all odd d >= 5; the odd-d lower bound only improves Welch by O(d^{-3/2}); U7 (0.4875) is weaker than the H8-derived (3*sqrt(2)+2)/14 = 0.4459 implicit in Jaming-Matolcsi (2015); and Theorem 3(b) adds little beyond Grassl (2004).

reproducibility.basis: The PDF states a concrete public GitHub URL and release tag (v1.0.0), gives complete proofs of Theorems 1-2, and prints exact U3, U5, U7 entries and skew-Cayley generators. However, NO actual SHA-256 hex digests appear anywhere in the PDF despite citing 16 SHA-256 certificates under certificates/MANIFEST.json, and Theorem 3(b) omits the 12 surviving exponent tuples in (Z/24Z)^5, preventing standalone verification of the 24^5 search from the PDF alone.

assessments.summary: This 10-page paper studies the real orthogonal minimax coherence mu_R(d) := min_{U in O(d)} ||U||_max and related MUB questions. Its core mathematical contribution (Theorems 1 and 2) is genuine, solid, and completely sound: using elementary polynomial identities, a three-row sign-parity obstruction, and Seidel-matrix spectral divisibility, the author proves mu_R(d) >= 1/sqrt(d-1) with complete conference-matrix rigidity for d = 4k+2 >= 6, and mu_R(d) >= 2/sqrt(4d-3) for odd d >= 3 with unique attainment at d = 3. These settle the conjectured value mu_R(d) = 1/sqrt(d-1) for all conference-matrix orders. However, major revision is required due to material framing overclaims, omitted foundational literature, and PDF reproducibility gaps: (1) the paper claims to 'resolve' mu_R(d) across the entire class d = 2 mod 4 and obtain an 'exact arithmetic dichotomy', whereas Belevitch-obstructed values (d=22,34,...) and non-prime-power conference-matrix existence remain open; (2) it omits Jaming & Matolcsi (2015) on flat orthogonal matrices (whose H_8-based d=7 matrix beats the paper's U7 witness) and Grassl (2004) / Haagerup on C^6 MUBs (Theorem 3(b)'s 12 rays are simply the classical 12th-root tensor products Y_2 tensor (M_1 U M_2) inside Grassl's 48-ray full-C^6 classification); and (3) no SHA-256 digests or explicit 12-ray tuples appear in the PDF despite referencing 16 SHA-256 certificates.
strengths: Theorem 1(a)-(b) gives an ingenious, completely elementary, self-contained proof that ||U||_max >= 1/sqrt(d-1) for all d = 4k+2 >= 6 and that equality holds if and only if sqrt(d-1)*U is a conference matrix up to column permutation, resolving a longstanding conjectured bound for conference-matrix orders such as d=6,10,14,18,26.

Theorem 2(a)-(b) establishes a sharp polynomial secant lower bound 2/sqrt(4d-3) for all odd d >= 3, strictly beating both Welch 1/sqrt(d) and the quadratic bound sqrt(2/(2d-1)), and cleanly proves via Seidel matrix spectral divisibility (s = sqrt(4d-3) | d => s | 3) that equality holds uniquely at d = 3.
Exact rational witnesses U5 = (1/11)circ(3,6,2,-6,6) and U7 = (1/2437)circ(-939,-522,1158,-384,1188,894,1042) are explicitly stated and check out exactly.

Section 5 is unusually candid about formal-verification boundaries, explicitly noting that Lean 4 checks only the scalar-algebraic, parity, divisibility, and finite-witness kernel while full matrix steps remain prose proofs.
weaknesses: The core proofs of Theorems 1 and 2, while very clean, are short (~4 pages) elementary arguments leaving open all odd d >= 5 and all Belevitch-obstructed d = 2 mod 4, and the odd-d lower bound only improves the Welch bound 1/sqrt(d) by O(d^{-3/2}).

Theorem 3(b) (a 24^5 brute-force/meet-in-the-middle ring search over Z[zeta_24]) is thematically disconnected from real orthogonal minimax coherence and merely re-certifies a 12th-root subset of Grassl's 2004 full-C^6 result without recognizing its simple C^2 tensor C^3 structure.
Important prior art (Jaming & Matolcsi 2015 on flat orthogonal matrices; Grassl 2004 / Haagerup on dimension-6 unbiased rays to {I_6, F_6}) is omitted from the bibliography.
No SHA-256 checksums or explicit 12-ray tuples of Theorem 3(b) are included in the PDF.
potential_errors: Minor framing/citation gap at d=7: U7 achieves 1188/2437 (~0.4875), which improves Householder (5/7) and is a valid rational circulant, but is strictly weaker than the elementary Hadamard-core matrix (A + ((1-2*sqrt(2))/7) J_7)/sqrt(8) from H_8 giving (3*sqrt(2)+2)/14 (~0.4459), consistent with Jaming & Matolcsi (2015), which is not cited.
Minor formatting typo on page 9: 'lean-DwarningAsError=true' is missing a space between 'lean' and '-DwarningAsError=true'.

Figure 2(c) colors all remaining sum-of-two-squares orders 6 <= d <= 102 uniformly as a distinct class from Belevitch-obstructed orders without explicitly indicating conference-matrix status (e.g. d=46, 66, 86), risking confusion between Belevitch's necessary condition and sufficiency.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorem 1(a)-(b): Unconditional lower bound ||U||_max >= 1/sqrt(d-1) and complete conference-matrix rigidity (eliminating |N0| >= 3, |N0| = 1, |N0| = 2) for all d = 4k+2 >= 6 via a three-row sign-parity obstruction and elementary polynomial identity.
Theorem 2(a)-(b): Secant linearization lower bound ||U||_max >= 2/sqrt(4d-3) for all odd d >= 3 and Seidel-matrix spectral divisibility proof of unique equality at d = 3.
unresolved_material_objections: Material framing overclaim in Abstract and Main Contributions 1: claiming to 'resolve the orthogonal minimax coherence problem mu_R(d) ... across the entire non-Hadamard residue class d = 2 (mod 4)' and claiming an 'exact arithmetic dichotomy' overstates Theorem 1. Exact values of mu_R(d) are left open for all Belevitch-obstructed orders (d = 22, 34, 58, 70, 78, 94, ...), as acknowledged in Remark 1(ii), and Belevitch's d-1 = a^2+b^2 condition is only necessary rather than sufficient for conference-matrix existence.

Material scholarly omission and overframing in Theorem 3(b) and Section 3: the paper omits Grassl (2004, quant-ph/0406175) and cyclic 6-roots classifications (Björck-Fröberg / Haagerup), which already enumerated all 48 rays in all of C^6 unbiased to {I_6, F_6} (12 classical 12th-root rays and 36 Björck rays) and ruled out a 4th MUB over all of C^6—not merely Z[zeta_24]—nor does the paper identify that V_{24} consists precisely of the elementary tensor-product rays Y_2 tensor (M_1 U M_2) in C^2 tensor C^3. It also omits Jaming & Matolcsi (2015, Acta Math. Hungar.), whose d = 3 mod 4 Hadamard-core construction already gives ||U||_max = (3*sqrt(2)+2)/14 ~ 0.4459 at d=7 (below U7's 1188/2437 ~ 0.4875).

PDF self-containment and reproducibility gap: the PDF cites '16 SHA-256 certificates under certificates/MANIFEST.json' but omits all actual SHA-256 hex digests, and Theorem 3(b) omits the explicit 12 surviving exponent tuples in (Z/24Z)^5, preventing independent verification of the computational claims from the PDF itself.

assessments.summary: This paper presents a rigorous mathematical and formally verified extension of Elder's recent framework connecting the sum-of-square-roots problem to exact semidefinite feasibility and Turnpike rulers. The authors establish a representation-independent Galois-theoretic barrier proving that any rank-1-Hessian Lorentz system has quadratic algebraic degree, ruling out polynomial-time reductions for radical sums with Kummer rank rho >= 2. They further construct a strictly minimal (k+2)-site planted ruler, prove sharp per-coordinate mixed-radix Freiman compression, and derive explicit Galois-norm margin lower bounds with constructive rational SDP witnesses. All theorems are fully verified in Lean 4 with zero sorry and zero Classical.choice.
strengths: Representation-independent classification of rank-1-Hessian Lorentz systems via Kummer theory and Besicovitch's theorem.
Strictly minimal (k+2)-site ruler eliminating auxiliary gap B.
Sharp per-coordinate mixed-radix Freiman compression with necessity proofs.
Complete formal verification in Lean 4 with zero sorry and zero Classical.choice.
weaknesses: Scope is restricted to sharpening and extending a single very recent preprint (Elder, Nov 2026).

correctness_confidence.basis: The main proofs of Theorem 1(a)-(b), Theorem 2(b), and Theorem 3(a) check out algebraically (including all 8 Table 1 norms and precision bounds). However, Theorem 1(c) overclaims ruling out all rational Corollary 7 reformulations: for k=2 (sqrt(2)+sqrt(3)), squaring once gives a 1D rank-1-Hessian-span feasibility system (x >= sqrt(6), 2x <= K^2-5). Also, Theorem 2(a) at k=1 and Theorem 3(b) cannot be fully verified from the PDF alone because gap_*, L_{a_i}, and U_{a_i} are undefined.

rigor.basis: Theorem 1(a) handles arbitrary dimension, polyhedral faces, and indefinite/singular quadrics cleanly. Yet rigor suffers from omitted definitions (sep, gap_*, w_j, L_{a_i}, U_{a_i}), omitting the (1,1) minor check in Sylvester's criterion (Thm 3b), calling vectors with zero coordinates 'strictly positive' (Thm 2b), understating total witness bit-length O(k*2^rho*L) as O(2^rho*L), and claiming Theorems 1-3 are 'constructively verified' when Lean only covers 20 elementary fragments.

In contrast, Theorems 2-3 are modest or elementary: dropping B from (k+3) to (k+2) sites, textbook per-coordinate mixed-radix bounds, a standard Galois-norm separation bound refined by Kummer rank rho (without citing prior SSR separation literature), and dyadic rounding.

significance.basis: Closely scoped as a reactive follow-up to Elder (arXiv:2611.34535v1) and OpenAI's Nov 2026 preprint, the paper's main contribution is ruling out extreme-value rank-1-Hessian-span Lorentz representations of the sum-of-square-roots threshold S whenever r_irr >= 2. Its broader impact is limited because the barrier does not rule out nonlinear-in-K feasibility encodings (e.g. k=2 by squaring) and the remaining ruler, radix, and rounding sharpenings are incremental.

assessments.summary: This 8-page follow-up to Elder (arXiv:2611.34535v1) addresses the Sum-of-Square-Roots threshold S vs K, Turnpike encodings, and rational SDP feasibility. Its main contribution is Theorem 1: any rational affine Lorentz system whose squared-residual Hessians span at most a 1D space has all attained rational-linear extreme values of degree <= 2 over Q, whereas [Q(S):Q] = 2^rho >= 4 for r_irr >= 2. Theorems 2-3 give modest sharpenings: dropping auxiliary gap B to get a (k+2)-site ruler, per-coordinate mixed radices 2M_j+1, Galois-norm margin bounds in Kummer rank rho, and dyadic strict-feasibility witnesses of exponent O(2^rho L). All Table 1 norms and exponents check out. However, major revision is needed for material overclaims and self-containedness gaps: (1) Theorem 1(c) and the Abstract overclaim ruling out all rational reformulations into OpenAI Corollary 7 for r_irr >= 2, overlooking nonlinear-in-K feasibility encodings (e.g. sqrt(2)+sqrt(3) <= K reduces to 1D Lorentz feasibility x >= sqrt(6), 2x <= K^2-5); (2) key objects from [2] (sep, gap_*, L_{a_i}, U_{a_i}, w_j) are undefined in the PDF, leaving Theorem 2(a) at k=1 and Sylvester's criterion in Theorem 3(b) (which omits the (1,1) minor) incomplete in isolation; and (3) Theorems 1-3 are overstated as constructively verified when Lean only covers 20 elementary lemmas.
strengths: Theorem 1(a) gives a clean, complete proof that any rational affine Lorentz system of arbitrary dimension N and constraint count m with Hessian span dimension <= 1 projects onto a rational polyhedron intersected with a single rational quadric t = x^T Q x, forcing every attained extreme value of a rational linear functional to have algebraic degree <= 2 over Q (carefully handling singular points and indefinite M|_R with alpha = 0).

Theorem 1(b) cleanly combines Kummer theory and Besicovitch's theorem to determine [Q(S):Q] = 2^rho and the exact equivalence rho <= 1 iff r_irr <= 1, illustrated accurately on dependent radicals like sqrt(2)+sqrt(3)+sqrt(6) (r_irr=3, rho=2, minimal polynomial x^4 - 22x^2 - 48x - 23).
Theorem 2(b) explicitly identifies the sharp threshold beta_j = 2M_j + 1 for carry-free mixed-radix Freiman preservation on product intervals [0, M_j] via simple explicit collision witnesses.

Theorem 3 sharpens the sum-of-square-roots Galois-norm lower bound exponent from 2^k - 1 or 2^{r_irr} - 1 to 2^rho - 1 and derives explicit dyadic denominator exponents q_Galois with all 8 instances in Table 1 verified exactly.
Concrete GitHub repository URL (p. 1) and deterministic SHA-256 manifest hash (p. 8) are provided in the PDF.
weaknesses: Reactive, tightly scoped 8-page follow-up to a single Nov 2026 preprint [2] with only 4 references, omitting all prior literature on Galois-norm / root-separation bounds for the Sum-of-Square-Roots problem (e.g., Tiwari, Burnikel-Fleischer-Mehlhorn-Schirra, Qian-Wang).
Theorems 2(a), 2(b), and 3(b) are mathematically elementary (removing an auxiliary gap B, mixed-radix non-carry bounds, and rounding sqrt(a_i) at dyadic precision D > k/|Delta|).
Theorem 2(a) strict minimality proof is slightly imprecise when K coincides with an existing pairwise distance of the (k+1)-site ruler.

Minor technical/notational slips: calling vectors with zero coordinates 'strictly positive' (Thm 2b), writing 'order-(2k+1)' for 2x2 blocks L_{a_i}, U_{a_i} (p. 2), overloading f_mix on labels and vectors (p. 5), and stating O(2^rho L) bit-length for k-dimensional vectors x in Q^k instead of O(k * 2^rho L) (Abstract).
The 16 individual SHA-256 certificate hashes and exact Lean theorem statements are omitted from the PDF (only one manifest hash is printed).
potential_errors: Theorem 1(c) and Abstract overclaim ruling out all rational reformulations into OpenAI's Corollary 7 for r_irr >= 2: for k=2 (e.g., sqrt(2)+sqrt(3) <= K, which is the paper's first counterexample), squaring once gives 2*sqrt(6) <= K^2 - 5, realizable as feasibility of the 1D rank-1-Hessian-span rational Lorentz system ||(12, 5x)||_2 <= 7x, ||0||_2 <= (K^2-5)-2x.

Theorem 2(a) claims strict minimality of k+2 sites among rulers realizing the k consecutive summand gaps and K, yet if K equals an existing pairwise distance of the (k+1)-site ruler (e.g., k=2, sqrt(a_1)=1, sqrt(a_2)=2, K=1), that (k+1)-site ruler (0,1,3) already has k+1 sites and contains K in Y with sep(Y)=1 <= |Delta|=2; strict minimality requires K to be an independent/additional consecutive gap.

Theorem 2(a) for k=1 relies crucially on a repeated-label triple (K, K, sqrt(a_1)+K) being valid in gap_*(Y) via [2, Eq. (1)], because for k=1 the 3-element multiset Y={sqrt(a_1), K, sqrt(a_1)+K} has no three-distinct-element triple yielding residual |Delta|; since gap_*(Y) is never defined in the PDF, this cannot be checked from the paper alone.

Proof of Theorem 3(b) invokes Sylvester's criterion for L_{a_i}(x_i) > 0 and U_{a_i}(x_i) > 0 by checking only det > 0 without stating the matrices or checking the (1,1) leading principal minor > 0 (and page 2 inaccurately calls the 2x2 blocks L_{a_i}, U_{a_i} 'order-(2k+1)' matrix pencils).
Theorem 2(b) calls the counterexample vectors u=(beta_1-1,0), v=(1,0), w=(0,1) 'strictly positive when beta_1 >= 2', whereas every vector has a zero coordinate (only f_mix is strictly positive).

Abstract states dyadic witnesses x in Q^k have explicit bit-length O(2^rho L), whereas O(2^rho L) is the per-coordinate bit-length and the full k-dimensional vector x has total bit-length O(k * 2^rho L).
strong_novelty_candidates: Representation-independent degree-2 algebraic barrier (Theorem 1(a),(c)) ruling out representing S = sum c_i sqrt(a_i) as an attained linear extreme value of any rational affine Lorentz system of arbitrary dimension whose squared-residual Hessians span at most a 1D space whenever r_irr >= 2.
unresolved_material_objections: Overclaim in Theorem 1(c) and Abstract: The paper claims 2^rho >= 4 > 2 'rules out every rational reformulation into OpenAI's Corollary 7' for all r_irr >= 2 (explicitly citing sqrt(2)+sqrt(3)). In fact, Theorem 1 only rules out representing S itself as an attained linear extreme value; for k=2 (including sqrt(2)+sqrt(3) <= K), squaring once reduces the decision problem to feasibility of a 1-dimensional (hence rank-1-Hessian-span) rational Lorentz system: ||(12, 5x)||_2 <= 7x and ||0||_2 <= (K^2-5)-2x.

Severe self-containedness and proof-completeness gaps from omitted external definitions: The PDF never defines sep(Y), gap_*(Y), w_j(u) / normalized radical rulers, or the affine PSD blocks L_{a_i}(x_i) and U_{a_i}(x_i) from [2]. Consequently, Theorem 2(a) at k=1 (which fails unless gap_*(Y) permits repeated labels) and Theorem 3(b) (whose Sylvester-criterion proof checks only the 2x2 determinant without defining the blocks or verifying the (1,1) principal minor > 0) cannot be verified from the PDF alone.

Overstatement of constructive formal verification: The Abstract presents Theorems 1-3 as 'three constructively verified theorems', and p. 4 cites 'Lean 4 Theorem 1' right after [Q(S):Q] = 2^rho >= 4 > 2, whereas the 20 dependency-free Lean lemmas only verify elementary polynomial/arithmetic identities and finite inequalities while the non-trivial components (Lagrange multipliers on polyhedral faces, Kummer theory, Besicovitch's theorem, algebraic integrality of Galois norms) are unformalized.
