assessments.summary: This paper presents an exceptional, rigorously verified mathematical sharpening of Cheval et al.'s recent breakthrough placing exact normal-form correlated equilibrium (NFCE) computation in PPAD for extensive-form games. The author establishes three major theorems: (1) an exponentially sharper rational LP gap using path-LCM denominators and unscaled-simplex column-Hadamard determinant bounds; (2) effective payoff-rank support compression and a closed-form two-player support collapse; and (3) arbitrary-m matching tree constructions that eliminate power-of-two restrictions, characterize exact b-ary branching optimality (proving ternary trees halve matching information sets), and establish leaf-count PPAD-completeness. All claims are backed by 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems (zero sorry) and 16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates.
strengths: Exponential reduction in oracle bit-precision via path-LCM denominator replacement (up to 632x-884x savings).
Elegant polynomial-time effective payoff-rank support compression reducing quadratic support to O(di) at low payoff rank.
Arbitrary-m matching tree construction eliminating the power-of-two restriction and slashing hardness tree sizes by 8.4x to 86.5x.
Exemplary formal verification and reproducibility with 20 Lean 4 theorems and 16 AST-audited zero-float certificates.
weaknesses: As a reactive follow-up to a very recent preprint (arXiv:2611.34897v1), the conceptual leap builds directly upon established machinery rather than introducing an entirely new foundational paradigm.
strong_novelty_candidates: Path-LCM rational LP gap and Cramer-Hadamard dimension exponent halving.
Effective payoff-rank support compression for sequence-form games.

correctness_confidence.basis: Core LP gap, Cramer-Hadamard bound, payoff-rank formula, b-ary counts, Table 2 benchmarks, and both barriers verify mathematically. However, Abstract/Table 1/Conclusion misclaim PPAD-completeness under kappa_N = floor(N^2/9) instead of Theorem 3(c)'s kappa_{N+} = max{kappa_d, kappa_N}, even though kappa_N is infeasible on M_m for all m >= 2. Also, Theorem 1(b) passes irrational epsilon*_Gamma without dyadic rounding, and Table 1 miswrites h + log D as h log D.

rigor.basis: Theorem 1(b)'s Cramer-Hadamard proof and Theorem 3(b)'s b-ary algebra are clear, but overall rigor is weakened by black-box deferral to [1] (Theorem 6, Algorithm 1, Lemmas 16-19). Theorem 2(a) omits explicit proofs of polynomial bit-growth during rational Gaussian elimination on W_i and prefix-conditioned factorization of Psi-tilde inside Algorithm 1. The Abstract's Theta(|Z|/h) claim omits regime hypotheses (D=O(1), log K=O(h)), and kappa_N vs kappa_{N+} is stated inconsistently.

novelty.basis: Reactive follow-up to a single Nov. 2026 preprint ([1]) importing all core PPAD reduction and oracle machinery. Proofs rely on elementary linear algebra (path-LCM, unscaled-simplex Cramer/Hadamard, payoff-weighted subspace projection) and elementary tree counting or short counterexamples. Still, payoff-rank compression K_eff, b in {2,3} optimality with ternary info-set halving, and the 2m^2 and 2q-player barriers are genuinely new observations over [1].

significance.basis: Eliminates an exponential |Z| bit-precision blowup on chance-heavy trees in [1]'s algorithm (632x denominator reduction at depth 10) and halves the Cramer-Hadamard exponent. Compresses quadratic support to O(d_i) at constant payoff rank, cuts PPAD-hardness tree sizes by 8.4x-86.5x, lowers the completeness threshold from r >= 5 to r >= 3, and clarifies why matching-tree and parallel-chance gadgets stall at 2m^2 and m^2. Scope remains tightly tied to [1].

reproducibility.basis: The PDF states a concrete public GitHub repository URL and names specific Lean, Python verifier, test, and manifest paths, plus explicit numerical benchmarks in Table 2 and explicit counterexamples. However, despite highlighting '16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates', neither actual 64-hex SHA-256 digests nor a pinned git commit hash appear anywhere in the PDF, and the upper endpoint of the '632x-884x at h=10' claim lacks specified parameters.

assessments.summary: A focused, reactive follow-up to Cheval et al. (arXiv:2611.34897v1, Nov. 2026) sharpening quantitative bounds in their PPAD algorithm and matching-tree hardness framework for exact NFCE in perfect-recall extensive-form games. Theorem 1 replaces the tree-wide denominator product B with the path-LCM L = lcm_{z,i} den(p_c(z)u_i(z)) and uses an unscaled-simplex Cramer-Hadamard bound to halve the dimension exponent while removing an exponential |Z| factor in oracle bit-precision on chance trees. Theorem 2 introduces an effective payoff-deviation rank r_i <= d_i compressing support to K_eff = min(prod_i(d_i+1), 1+sum_i(d_i+1)r_i), plus the identity 2(K-kappa_d) = d_1^2+d_2^2+(d_1-d_2)^2. Theorem 3 extends binary matching trees to arbitrary m >= 2 (8.4x-86.5x smaller hardness trees), characterizes b-ary optimality (node slope 6 iff b in {2,3}; leaf slope 3 at b=2), proves completeness under kappa_{N+} for r >= 3, and exhibits 2m^2 correlated and m^2 parallel-chance barriers. However, all deep results are imported black-box from [1], Theorem 2(a) omits explicit prefix-factorization and bit-growth proofs, the Abstract, Table 1, and Conclusion materially misstate completeness under kappa_N (infeasible on M_m) instead of kappa_{N+}, and no concrete SHA-256 digests appear in the PDF.
strengths: Clean identification of path-LCM L = lcm_{z,i} den(p_c(z)u_i(z)) and unscaled-simplex Cramer-Hadamard argument in Theorem 1(b), strictly improving upon eta_CHPS for all K >= 1, B >= L >= 2 and avoiding exponential chance-tree bit blowup.
Payoff-weighted deviation subspace projection W_i in Theorem 2(a) genuinely compresses support from O(d_i^2) to O(d_i r_i) and unifies the two-player product bound inside K_eff.

Exact arbitrary-m full binary matching tree construction (|V|=6m-5, N=3m-2, d_i=m-1) and complete characterization of b-ary branching optimality (node slope 6 iff b in {2,3}, ternary halving |I_i|; leaf slope 3 uniquely at b=2).

Explicit, self-contained 2m^2 Battle of the Sexes correlated barrier (c=1/18, Nash regret 1/12) and 2q-player parallel chance-branch synchronization barrier (m^2 < m^{2q}) cleanly pinning down the structural limits of [1]'s hardness paradigm.
weaknesses: Reactive follow-up entirely scoped to a single recent preprint ([1]); all deep game-theoretic machinery (PPAD oracle reduction, sequential Carathéodory BFS, and entropy/Pinsker hardness reduction) is imported verbatim from [1], while the new proofs are elementary linear algebra, tree counting, and short counterexamples.

Material discrepancy between kappa_N (Abstract, Table 1, Conclusion) and kappa_{N+} (Theorem 3(c)); plus missing dyadic rounding for irrational epsilon*_Gamma and misstated Theta(K(h log D + log K)) entry in Table 1.
Compressed exposition in Theorem 2(a) omits explicit prefix-factorization formulas and Gaussian elimination bit-growth verification.

Despite prominently advertising '16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates', the PDF prints no actual 64-hex SHA-256 checksums or pinned git commit SHA, and does not specify what benchmark parameters yield the '884x' figure at h=10.
potential_errors: Abstract, Table 1, and Conclusion claim PPAD-completeness under kappa_N = floor(N^2/9), whereas on every matching tree M_m (m >= 2) we have N = 3m - 2 and kappa_N = floor((3m-2)^2/9) <= m^2 - 1 < m^2 <= |supp(mu)|, so no exact NFCE of support <= kappa_N exists; only kappa_{N+} = max{kappa_d, kappa_N} (Theorem 3(c)) is valid.

Theorem 1(b) sets epsilon*_Gamma := 0.5 * eta_sharp(K, L) = 0.5 / (sqrt(K)(1 + KL^2)^{K/2} L), which is generically irrational and cannot be passed directly to Etessami's binary-accuracy Nash oracle without rounding down to a dyadic rational (e.g., 2^{-ceil(log_2(1/epsilon*_Gamma))}).

Table 1 reports the new oracle bit budget on depth-h trees as Theta(K(h log D + log K)) instead of Theta(K(h + log D + log K)), and the Abstract's Theta(|Z|/h) speedup ratio implicitly assumes fixed D (or log D = O(h)) and log K = O(h) without stating or proving these conditions in Section 3.

Theorem 2(a) does not explicitly prove that exact rational Gaussian elimination for {w_{i,l}} preserves polynomial bit-lengths or write out the per-stage prefix factorization E_{alpha_{>t}}[Psi-tilde(tau_{<=t}, tau_{>t})] needed when calling Algorithm 1 of [1].
strong_novelty_candidates: Path-LCM denominator L combined with unscaled-simplex column-Hadamard gap bound halving the dimension exponent and eliminating the exponential |Z| factor on chance trees.
Polynomial-time effective payoff-deviation rank compression K_eff = min(prod_i(d_i+1), 1 + sum_i(d_i+1)r_i) via sequence-form basis projection onto W_i.
Exact b-ary matching-tree node/leaf slope optimality showing ternary trees (b=3) match binary node count 6m-5 while halving matching information sets.
Two explicit no-go counterexamples showing matching-tree decoders fail at support 2m^2 (c=1/18) and disjoint chance-selected matching pairs collapse from m^{2q} to m^2 via cross-pair synchronization.
unresolved_material_objections: Material overclaim in Abstract, Table 1, and Conclusion: PPAD-completeness is claimed under the pure leaf-count bound kappa_N = floor(N^2/9), whereas Theorem 3(c) only establishes PPAD-completeness under kappa_{N+} = max{kappa_d, kappa_N}. For every matching tree M_m (m >= 2), kappa_N = floor((3m-2)^2/9) <= m^2 - 1 < m^2, while every exact NFCE on M_m has support >= m^2 (Theorem 2(b)), making exact NFCE under kappa_N infeasible (not even total).

Incomplete proof details and irrational oracle accuracy: Theorem 2(a) relies on [1, Section 3.2 & Algorithm 1] without explicitly deriving polynomial bit-lengths for exact rational Gaussian elimination on W_i or writing out the player-prefix factorization E_{alpha_{>t}}[Psi-tilde(tau_{<=t}, tau_{>t})]. Theorem 1(b) treats [1, Theorem 6] as a black box and passes a generically irrational epsilon*_Gamma = 0.5 * eta_sharp(K, L) to a binary-accuracy oracle without dyadic rounding.

Asymptotic and benchmark imprecisions: Table 1 misstates the depth-h oracle bit budget as Theta(K(h log D + log K)) instead of Theta(K(h + log D + log K)), the Abstract's Theta(|Z|/h) asymptotic speedup is stated without proof or regime assumptions (D = O(1), log K = O(h)), and the 884x upper bound in '632x-884x at h=10' lacks parameter specification.

reproducibility.basis: Accompanied by a complete Lean 4 formalization and a zero-float Python verification script emitting 16 SHA-256 certificates under MANIFEST.json in the GitHub repository.

assessments.summary: This paper establishes three exact, closed-form separation theorems linking analytic, geometric, partition, and slice ranks across structured multilinear tensors in finite fields. It proves an unbounded characteristic-2 versus odd-characteristic phase transition for complete 3-hypergraph tensors, derives universal rational bias formulas for the 3x3 determinant and matrix multiplication via q-binomial rank counts, and proves an unbounded 2m-tensor separation. The proofs are mathematically rigorous and backed by a 20-theorem Lean 4 formalization and zero-float Python verifiers.
strengths: Complete, rigorous mathematical proofs for all three main tensor families.
Fully formalized in Lean 4.36.0 with zero axioms/sorry and verified by zero-float Python scripts.
Exact rational bias formulas and characteristic phase transition classifications.
weaknesses: Specialized scope focused on specific algebraic tensor families and hypergraphs rather than general black-box tensors.

correctness_confidence.basis: All closed-form formulas, inequalities, and numerical values—including F_2 biases of K_n^(3), F_3 biases up to K_6^(3) (8821/531441), det_3, M_2, the M_n strict deficit, the F_2^7 histograms of omega_Fano (29/512) and omega_max (95/2048), and T_d^(2m)—were independently verified from first principles. Minor expositional slips remain (omitted subcase u_3!=0, u_1*u_2=0 in Thm 1(b); implicit multilinearity in pr/sr; external proof reliance in Thm 1(b) F_3 and Thm 2(c)).

rigor.basis: Core analytic proofs (Thm 1(a), Thm 2(a)-(b), Thm 3) are sound and Section 5 candidly restricts Lean coverage to cleared-denominator algebraic/arithmetic tails. Rigor is weakened because Thm 1(b)'s F_3 values and all of Thm 2(c) rely on unproved external computations, Proof of Thm 1(b) omits u_3!=0 with u_1=0 or u_2=0, Sec 1 omits multilinearity in pr/sr, and Thm 2(c) overstates two 7D forms as an atlas in Lambda^3(F_2^n).

However, the conceptual ingredients (inclusion-exclusion + Tao's lemma, gr(M_n), sr(det_3)=3, I_{d^m} flattening of product inner products, Cohen-Helminck 3-forms) are standard or imported, and the new proofs are short elementary linear algebra or probability calculations.

significance.basis: Provides crisp, exact finite-field benchmark separations quantifying known asymptotic/general phenomena (char-2 vs odd-p phase transition on K_n^(3), finite-field deficit gr(M_n)-ar_{F_p}(M_n)>0, and order-2m pr-vs-sr gap with exact bias). Valuable as a clean technical reference note, though it neither resolves an established hard open problem nor introduces significant new proof methodology.

However, zero actual SHA-256 hashes (or commit SHAs) appear in the PDF despite prominently advertising 16 SHA-256 certificates, and verifying Thm 1(b) (F_3) and Thm 2(c) requires running unprinted external scripts.

assessments.summary: This 9-page note derives exact closed-form bias formulas and finite-field rank separations for four structured multilinear tensor families: complete 3-hypergraphs K_n^(3), det_3, matrix multiplication M_n (plus two 7D alternating 3-forms in Lambda^3(F_2^7)), and balanced 2m-tensors T_d^(2m). Independent first-principles verification confirms that the stated closed forms, signs, asymptotic limits, and numerical values (including F_3 biases of K_3^(3)..K_6^(3) and the F_2^7 rank histograms of omega_Fano and omega_max) are mathematically accurate. However, under a strict anti-inflation standard, the paper's actual mathematical depth is that of a modest technical note: every analytic proof relies on elementary linear algebra, inclusion-exclusion, quadratic completion, or independent inner-product probability built atop imported theorems (Tao's diagonal lemma, Kopparty-Moshkovitz-Zuiddam's geometric rank of M_n, Lovett's ar<=pr, Cohen-Helminck's 3-forms). Moreover, the PDF leaves the F_3 crossing (Thm 1(b)) and all of Thm 2(c) without analytic proofs, overstates two 7D examples as an 'atlas in Lambda^3(F_2^n)', omits a subcase in the K_3^(3) lower-bound proof, omits multilinearity from the pr/sr definitions, and omits the advertised SHA-256 digests from the manuscript itself.
strengths: Exact closed-form classification of the contraction-rank spectrum {0, 2, 2*floor((n-1)/2)} and bias_{F_2}(K_n^(3)) = 1/8 + 7 * 2^{-(2*floor((n-1)/2)+3)} for all n >= 3, sharply contrasting with sr_{F_p}(K_n^(3)) >= n - 3 over every odd prime p >= 3.

Clean q-binomial bias formula (11) for n x n matrix multiplication M_n together with an elementary, self-contained proof via square completion (15) and factor comparison (16) that ar_{F_p}(M_n) < ceil(3n^2/4) = gr(M_n) holds strictly for all finite prime fields F_p and all n >= 2 while recovering the asymptotic limit ceil(3n^2/4).

Exact closed-form bias formula (20) for the balanced 2m-tensor T_d^(2m) over all finite prime fields F_p, giving an explicit strict separation ar_{F_p} < 1 = pr < d = sr and exponential decay of the d->infinity analytic rank ceiling in m.

Independent mathematical audit confirms all stated closed-form formulas, asymptotic limits, Table 1 rational entries, and Figure 1-3 numerical curves are mathematically true, including the F_3 biases of K_3^(3)..K_6^(3) and the F_2^7 rank spectra of omega_Fano and omega_max.

Section 5 is commendably transparent about the exact scope boundary of the Lean formalization, noting that Lean checks only cleared-denominator algebraic and arithmetic identities while the linear algebra and character sums are proved on paper.
weaknesses: Proof depth is uniformly elementary: all new derivations are short undergraduate linear algebra, quadratic square-completion, or independent product-probability calculations layered on top of imported core theorems from Tao [13], Kopparty-Moshkovitz-Zuiddam [8], Lovett [9], and Cohen-Helminck [2].

Several subresults already reflect standard/folklore observations (e.g., sr(det_3) = 3, gr(det_3) = 2, pr(T_d^(2m)) = 1 < d = sr(T_d^(2m)) via I_{d^m} flattening, and lim_{p->infty} ar_{F_p}(M_n) = gr(M_n) = ceil(3n^2/4)).

Unproved computational delegation inside main theorems: Theorem 1(b)'s odd-characteristic crossing ar_{F_3}(K_6^(3)) > 3 and all of Theorem 2(c) are proved only by citing external Python runs (cert02, cert08, cert09) rather than self-contained mathematical arguments, even though short hand proofs exist.

Presentation/packaging inflation risk: Lean 4 formalization covers only cleared-denominator identities and basic arithmetic bounds (thm01-thm20), not matrix ranks, character orthogonality, or Kronecker flattenings, and the advertised SHA-256 hashes do not appear in the PDF.
potential_errors: Proof of Theorem 1(b) (p. 4): when proving rank(M_u) >= 2 for u in ker(l) with at least two nonzero coordinates, the parenthetical explicitly lists only (u_3 = 0 and u_1, u_2 != 0) and (u_1 u_2 u_3 != 0), omitting the case u_3 != 0 with u_1 = 0 or u_2 = 0 (e.g., u = (1,0,1)), even though the stated top-left 2x2 minor -u_3^2 != 0 covers all u_3 != 0.

Section 1 (p. 2): partition rank (pr) and slice rank (sr) are defined via arbitrary summands g(x_S) h(x_{\bar S}) without specifying multilinearity, whereas the proofs in Sections 2 and 4 (ker(l), Kronecker flattening rank) treat slices as multilinear forms.

Abstract (p. 1): describes {0, 2, 2*floor((n-1)/2)} as an 'exact three-value set' for all n >= 3, whereas for n in {3, 4} it degenerates to the two-value set {0, 2} (though Theorem 1(a) states set membership accurately).
Section 5 (p. 7): minor CLI typo 'lean-DwarningAsError=true' missing a space after 'lean'.
strong_novelty_candidates: Elementary proof of the strict finite-field deficit ar_{F_p}(M_n) < ceil(3n^2/4) = gr(M_n) for all primes p >= 2 and all n >= 2 via q-binomial rank stratification and factor bound (16).
Closed-form contraction-rank spectrum and bias_{F_2}(K_n^(3)) exhibiting an unbounded characteristic-2 vs. odd-characteristic slice-rank phase transition on the complete 3-uniform hypergraph tensor.
Closed-form finite-field bias formula 1 - ((p-1)/p)^(m-1) (1 - p^-d)^m for T_d^(2m) quantifying the ar < 1 = pr < d = sr separation.
unresolved_material_objections: Material overclaim and missing proofs in Theorem 2(c) and Theorem 1(b): Theorem 2(c) and the Abstract claim an 'Exact Lambda^3(F_2^n) alternating 3-form atlas', yet the PDF only exhibits two forms in Lambda^3(F_2^7) (omega_Fano without specifying the PG(2,2) labeling and omega_max) with no orbit classification for Lambda^3(F_2^n) and no analytic proof in the PDF (relying solely on external Python certificates cert08 and cert09). Likewise, the F_3 bias values for K_3^(3)..K_6^(3) witnessing ar_{F_3} > 3 in Theorem 1(b) lack any written derivation in the PDF (relying solely on cert02). Either supply self-contained proofs/tables in the PDF or accurately scope Theorem 2(c) to two verified 7-dimensional examples.

Also clarify that partition/slice rank summands in Section 1 are multilinear, and correct 'three-value set' in the Abstract for n in {3, 4}.

correctness_confidence.basis: The algebraic and combinatorial arguments are fully substantiated, supported by rigorous casework, and backed by a zero-import Lean 4 formalization and exact Python verification.

rigor.basis: The paper provides exhaustive combinatorial reductions, heavy-line elimination lemmas, and structure-theorem cross-splitting analysis with exceptional logical precision.

novelty.basis: Establishes the first general upper bound for the large Davenport constant of the Heisenberg group Hp3 for all odd p >= 5, strictly separating it from the Loewy length.

significance.basis: Resolves a long-standing open problem in additive group combinatorics and zero-sum theory regarding non-abelian nilpotent groups of exponent p.

assessments.summary: This paper investigates the large Davenport constant D(H_p^3) of the Heisenberg group of order p^3 and exponent p for odd primes. It proves the general bounds 3p - 1 <= D(H_p^3) <= 4p - 4, which strictly separates D(H_p^3) from its Loewy length 4p - 3 (in sharp contrast to M_27). It also establishes new lower bounds for the short-subsequence invariants eta and s. The methodology combines symplectic exponential coordinates, Cauchy-Davenport contraction, heavy-line elimination, and property B structure-theorem cross-splitting. All results are corroborated by a zero-import Lean 4 formalization and exact computational verifications.
strengths: Completely eliminates the previous upper bound 5p - 4 down to 4p - 4 using novel heavy-line elimination and structure-theorem cross-splitting.
Provides two explicit, non-isomorphic extremal minimal product-one sequences of length 3p - 1 witnessing the lower bound.
Fully mechanized zero-import Lean 4 formalization alongside rigorous computational verification across small primes.
weaknesses: The analysis involves intricate combinatorial case distinctions, particularly in eliminating residual structural obstructions (O1) and (O2) for p >= 5.
Exact tightness at 3p - 1 remains open as Conjecture 6.1 for p >= 5, leaving a small remaining structural gap.
strong_novelty_candidates: The symplectic exponential coordinate framework reducing word products to affine functionals of ordered areas in F_p^2.
Heavy-line elimination and structure-theorem cross-splitting lemmas for zero-sum sequences in nilpotent p-groups.
Zero-import Lean 4 verification of non-abelian zero-sum invariants.

correctness_confidence.basis: All main theorems and lemmas hold after line-by-line verification of group identities, Cauchy-Davenport bounds, and p=3,5 edge cases. A minor expositional slip on p. 13 omits citing the active Lemma 4.1 bound m_1+c <= 2p-2 to exclude (p,p-1,p-1) at c=p-1.

rigor.basis: Arguments are generally careful and self-contained, handling boundary regimes (such as p=3, c=0, |S|=9 and p=5, L=3^6*2) explicitly. Minor polish issues include the omitted Lemma 4.1 citation on p. 13 and stating Lemma 2.2(b) without explicitly invoking it later.

novelty.basis: While building directly on Volkmann's exponential-coordinate order-value growth (Lemma 2.1) and Reiher's Property B, the three-set pigeonhole criterion on Z(G), heavy-line elimination, Property-B cross-splitting (Lemma 4.2), and fiber-doubled lifting for eta and s are original.

significance.basis: Lowers D(H_{p^3}) from 5p-4 to 4p-4 for all odd primes p>=3, strictly separating it from the Loewy length 4p-3, gives a conceptual proof of D(H_27)=8, and improves lower bounds for eta and s; however, the conjectured exact value 3p-1 and upper bounds for eta, s remain open.

reproducibility.basis: All mathematical proofs are explicit and verifiable from first principles modulo standard cited theorems (Reiher's Property B and Kemnitz theorems, Jennings' formula), complemented by explicit extremal witnesses and described Lean 4 core checks and Python DP verification.

assessments.summary: The manuscript investigates the large Davenport constant D(H_{p^3}) and short-subsequence invariants eta(H_{p^3}), s(H_{p^3}) for the Heisenberg group of order p^3 and odd prime exponent p. Building on symplectic exponential coordinates and Volkmann's order-value growth lemma, it introduces a three-set pigeonhole splitting criterion on Z(H_{p^3}), heavy-line elimination (Lemma 4.1), and a cross-splitting lemma using Reiher's Property B structure theorem (Lemma 4.2) to prove 3p-1 <= D(H_{p^3}) <= 4p-4 < 4p-3 = L(H_{p^3}) for all odd p >= 3. This settles D(H_27) = 8 conceptually and strictly separates D(H_{p^3}) from the Loewy length for all odd p. For p >= 5, Theorem 1.2 narrows the remaining [3p, 4p-4] gap to two explicit obstructions (O1)-(O2), and Theorem 1.3 proves eta(H_{p^3}) >= 7p-6 and s(H_{p^3}) >= 8p-7. All proofs check out mathematically, with one minor expositional omission on p. 13 in Case 3 (t=3) easily fixed by citing Lemma 4.1's m_1+c <= 2p-2.
strengths: Improves the uniform upper bound on D(H_{p^3}) from 5p-4 to 4p-4 for all odd primes p >= 3, strictly separating D(H_{p^3}) from the Loewy length 4p-3 = D_ord(H_{p^3}) in contrast to M_27.
Provides a purely conceptual, computer-free proof that D(H_27) = 8, carefully handling every p = 3, c = 0, |S| = 9 boundary case.

Constructs two explicit Aut(H_{p^3})-inequivalent minimal product-one sequences S^(1) and S^(2) of length 3p-1, and clean fiber-doubled witnesses T_eta and T_s establishing eta(H_{p^3}) >= 7p-6 and s(H_{p^3}) >= 8p-7.

Property-B cross-splitting (Lemma 4.2) and heavy-line elimination (Lemma 4.1) are technically clean and yield a concrete structural reduction of [3p, 4p-4] for p >= 5 to two explicit obstructions (O1)-(O2).
Transparently specifies the exact scope of the Lean 4.36.0 core formalization and Python DP checks without overclaiming mechanized coverage of the main theorems.
weaknesses: Does not resolve the conjectured exact value D(H_{p^3}) = 3p-1 for p >= 5, leaving a linear-width gap [3p-1, 4p-4] and the two structural obstructions (O1)-(O2) open.
Provides only lower bounds for eta(H_{p^3}) and s(H_{p^3}) with no upper bounds.

The residual class (O2) in Theorem 1.2 could be sharpened slightly near the upper endpoint 4p-4 (for instance, three-line triples at |S| = 4p-4 with reducible L_1 also split under the same argument used in Theorem 1.1).
Minor expositional issues: omitted invocation of Lemma 4.1 (m_1 + c <= 2p-2) on p. 13 when deducing m_1 = m_2 = p and c <= p-2, and stating Lemma 2.2(b) without explicitly invoking it later.
potential_errors: Page 13, Case 3 (t=3), second sub-bullet: The claim that m_3 <= m_2 <= m_1 <= p, m_1 + m_2 + m_3 + c >= 4p-3, and c <= p-1 force m_1 = m_2 = p, m_3 >= p-1, and c >= p-3 omits the solution (m_1, m_2, m_3, c) = (p, p-1, p-1, p-1). That configuration is already ruled out by Lemma 4.1's bound m_1 + c <= 2p-2 (stated at the start of Case 3 on p. 12), which forces c <= p-2 whenever m_1 = p, and is also ruled out by Lemma 2.2(a)+(c); citing m_1 + c <= 2p-2 there also avoids redundantly carrying c = p-1 into the subsequent paragraph.
Page 5, Lemma 2.2(b): The arithmetic pairing lemma is proved cleanly but never explicitly referenced elsewhere in the paper (its mechanism is restated inline inside Lemma 4.2).
strong_novelty_candidates: Strict separation D(H_{p^3}) <= 4p-4 < 4p-3 = L(H_{p^3}) for all odd primes p >= 3 and conceptual proof of D(H_27) = 8.
Three-set pigeonhole splitting criterion on the central fiber Z(H_{p^3}) (Lemma 2.2(d)) combined with heavy-line elimination (Lemma 4.1) and Property-B cross-splitting (Lemma 4.2).
Exact structural reduction of the remaining [3p, 4p-4] interval for p >= 5 to obstructions (O1)-(O2) (Theorem 1.2).
Fiber-doubled lifting witnesses T_eta and T_s establishing eta(H_{p^3}) >= 7p-6 and s(H_{p^3}) >= 8p-7 for all odd primes p >= 3 (Theorem 1.3).
